courses.description: This course develops and uses a framework for making judgments in a financial statement auditing context. The audit judgment framework includes a deep understanding of concepts such as the audit risk model, audit evidence, audit sampling and others. This framework is applied to most of the financial statement accounts found in a typical business including revenue, receivables, payables, inventory, fixed assets and other accounts. Other topics covered include professional ethics for accountants and the legal and professional environment affecting financial statement audits.

courses.subject: ANTHR

courses.description: This course has two related foci. First, students will practice the methods of ethnographic research, including best practices for participant observation interviewing, among other methods. To this end, students will conduct a mini-ethnography over the course of the semester. Second, students will develop and write a research proposal for the research they will carry out in their field schools. This research proposal will include a research question, a review of the literature that will motivate the research question, a description of the site where the research will be carried out, and an outline of the methods to be used in data collection and analysis. Students will be able to explain ethical research practices and they may need to pursue IRB approval as well.

courses.subject: ASL

courses.description: This course will provide students with novice-level communication, focusing on appropriate topics in beginning conversation.  It provides the opportunity to practice developed skills in a conventional setting.

courses.subject: ASL

courses.subject: ASL

courses.subject: ASL

courses.description: This course instructs students on the appropriate use of fingerspelling and numbers in ASL, including defining the rules and expectations of their incorporation into the language.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: American Sign Language Intermediate Conversation
courses.description: This course provides conversational opportunities for ASL students to engage at the intermediate-level on topics related to family, work, school, and personal interests.

courses.subject: ASL

courses.description: The fifth in a series of five courses. Focuses on developing advanced language skills in ASL that reflect an Advanced Low level. Deaf Culture and linguistic aspects of ASL will be taught.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: Deaf Literature
courses.description: This course is designed to provide ASL students opportunities to view and discuss creative works in the language, analyze artistic styles, and incorporate these examples into their own literary productions.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: ASL Special Topics
courses.description: This course will explore a variety of special topics in ASL and/or Deaf Culture such as recreation, math, women's studies, medicine, and religion.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: American Sign Language Advanced Conversation
courses.description: This course provides advanced conversation opportunities for students by exploring topics outside of self, including community and global events.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: History of Modern Deaf Culture
courses.description: This course explores the emergence of a Deaf school in the United States and the evolution of Deaf culture from 1817 to the present.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: Advanced Language Proficiency through Cultural Studies: ASL
courses.description: This course will focus on advanced-level grammar and language by means of receptive and expressive activities pertaining to local and global issues. Designed for returned missionaries or equivalent experience.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: Introduction to American Sign Language Linguistics
courses.description: This course explores the dynamics of ASL linguistics, including basic similarities between ASL and other languages.  Specific linguistic concepts and vocabulary will be addressed.

courses.subject: ASL
courses.title: Interpreting 1
courses.description: Building basic interpreting skills. Code of Ethics, interpreting protocol, and interpreting issues.

courses.subject: ASL

courses.description: Students will explore the ASL interpreting profession and related issues, including the Code of Professional Conduct and interpreting protocol.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Principles of Biology
courses.description: Introductory course for general education students.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Field Biology
courses.description: Field Biology is an introduction to the methods of outdoor field research and curation of natural history specimens. Students will  learn basic methods of fieldwork. Topics include an introduction to common plant and animal species and communities of Utah, documentation of field notes, and specimen collection and curation. Instruction will be primarily through extended field trips.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Biology Teaching and Learning
courses.description: Teaching Assistants will be prepared with the skills and knowledge necessary to mentor the students they serve. Students will develop a greater understanding of how to facilitate learning by exploring learning theories and instructional practices.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Biology
courses.description: General biology course with laboratory for biology majors.  Introduction to disciplines in the life sciences including methods for scientific inquiry, biochemical dynamics, cell structure and function, evolutionary theory, bioenergetics, and ecological interactions.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
courses.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a major driver of medical advances, improving diagnosis, treatment and therapeutics. Future health-care professionals must be familiar with the goals, methods and limitations of AI and machine learning. This course examines how these techniques can drive innovation and improve medical care.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics
courses.description: This course introduces the field of bioinformatics at an introductory level. Students learn about the field and gain experience with computer programming at a level that provides a foundation for future learning.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Bioinformatics Skills: Workflows
courses.description: Students will learn concepts and skills related to operating systems generally, the Linux operating system, and using computational workflows to execute bioinformatics software.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Introduction to Mentored Research
courses.description: Introduction to mentored research experiences under faculty supervision.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Biological Diversity: Animals
courses.description: Comparative organization and evolutionary significance of morphological, physiological, reproductive, and ecological differences in invertebrates and vertebrates.  Laboratory included.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Biological Diversity: Plants
courses.description: Comparative organization and evolutionary significance of morphological, physiological, reproductive, and ecological differences in fungi, algae, and principal groups of land plants.  Laboratory included.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Field Botany
courses.description: Recognition, characteristics, and uses of common trees and shrubs.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Curation of Biodiversity Collections
courses.description: Rationale, methods, and standards of curation for organismal specimens across the tree of life with an emphasis on physical preservation, responsible specimen use & loans, database standards, and digitization methods for electronic dissemination of specimen data.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Evolutionary Medicine
courses.description: Evolutionary medicine is the field of study of how Darwinian principles can be applied to understand problems in medicine and public health. Students will learn foundational principles of evolution including genetic processes of adaptation and genetic drift, the origin of life, and the hominin fossil record. With this foundational understanding, students will explore modern examples of evolution and human health problems.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Statistical Analysis for Biologists
courses.description: Students will learn concepts and applications of statistics and their specific application to research questions spanning diverse subfields of biology. Students will perform these analyses using the R statistical software.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Exploration of Teaching in Biological Sciences
courses.description: Field-based initial teaching experience directed at helping prospective teachers experience demands and opportunities associated with teaching secondary students.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Comparative Animal Physiology
courses.description: We will compare different animals' anatomical and physiological solutions to organismal needs (e.g., energy metabolism, sensory processes, reproduction, etc.) considering their different environments and evolutionary pressures.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Advanced Scientific Writing and Communication
courses.description: The effective process of written, oral, and visual scientific communication and development of communication skills for scientific and professional audiences. Employment of appropriate research tools and processes in identifying and evaluating sources, and following professional conventions in written and oral communication.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Ecology
courses.description: Distribution and abundance of organisms and their interactions with the physical and biotic components of the earth.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Computational Cancer Biology
courses.description: Examine the altered cellular phenotypes of cancer through a computational exploration of molecular and clinical data, comparing and contrasting different cancer types.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Bioinformatics Algorithms
courses.description: In this course, students learn theory and concepts of bioinformatics algorithms that are used in the field. They gain experience implementing these algorithms and applying them. These algorithms are used in diverse biological disciplines, including genome assembly, phylogenetics, multiple sequence alignment, next-generation sequencing read mapping, gene-expression analysis, and mass-spectrometry analysis.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: (Bio-MMBio-PWS) Genomics
courses.description: Current analysis of genes and genomes; computational approaches for interpreting genomic data, including genome sequencing and annotation, gene expression and the transcriptome, functional genomics, metagenomics, and genetic variation and SNPs.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Bioethics
courses.description: In-depth lecture and small group discussion of varied bioethical issues. LDS Church positions emphasized when appropriate.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Plant Development and Morphology
courses.description: Principles of development and morphology as applied to flowering plants from the seed to flowering

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Teaching Methods and Instruction in Biology
courses.description: Developing meaningful and engaging instruction for secondary students in biological sciences; developing critical thinking, problem solving, literacy, and democratic character; assessing learner performance.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Practicum in Biology Teaching
courses.description: Implementing meaningful and engaging instruction for secondary students in biology; developing critical thinking, problem solving, literacy, and democratic character; assessing learner performance.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Classroom Management and Laboratory Safety
courses.description: Current theory, research, and application in classroom management; creating positive teacher-student and peer relationships; developing optimal learning environments.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Preveterinary Preceptorship
courses.description: Supervised on-the-job exposure to veterinary medicine under a clinical setting, supplemented with academic assignments.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Academic Internship
courses.description: This course provides credit for students engaged in internship opportunities within the university or with research or industry groups outside of the university. Students will gain practical skills through mentored experiences in authentic environments.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Conservation Biology
courses.description: This course will explore key biological frameworks, including the history of conservation biology, patterns of biodiversity, causes of extinction and population decline, methods for population restoration, conservation genetics, and the role of conservation in sustaining ecosystem services. We will also study the human aspects of conservation, covering topics such as values and ethics in conservation, conservation economics and sustainable development.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Evolutionary Biology
courses.description: Intensive examination of evolution as the conceptual cornerstone of biology.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Plant Classification and Identification
courses.description: Principles of plant systematics, taxonomy, and classification, emphasizing family recognition by sight, terminology, and use of identification keys to the temperate flora.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Entomology
courses.description: External morphology, natural history, evolution, distribution, and phylogeny of insects.  Insect collection required.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Ichthyology
courses.description: Fish systematics, evolution, morphology, distribution, and natural history.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Herpetology
courses.description: Reptile and amphibian evolution, systematics, morphology, distribution, and natural history. Lab emphasizes taxonomy, classification, and distribution of western U.S. species.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Mammalogy
courses.description: Mammalian diversity, evolution, distribution, and natural history. Two three-day field trips required.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Capstone in Biodiversity and Conservation
courses.description: Students will apply principles of biodiversity and conservation to complete a complex project that integrates their disciplinary understanding to address a broad issue in conservation or biodiversity research. This culminating experience will allow students to create a project that will facilitate their transition into a post baccalaureate environment.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Marine Biology
courses.description: Principles of physical and biological oceanography, biodiversity, and ecology of numerous ocean habitats.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Plant Ecology
courses.description: Fundamental  principles governing interactions among plants and their environments with respect to their success. Students will be able to apply their knowledge to land management, conservation and agriculture.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Genetics of Human Disease
courses.description: Examining the application of genetics to understanding and treatment of human disease.  Functional consequences of mutations; use of model organisms; linkage and association analysis of complex traits; pharmacogenetics; ethical considerations.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Capstone in Bioinformatics
courses.description: Students will apply principles of bioinformatics to complete a complex project that integrates their disciplinary understanding to address a broad, integrative computational problem. This culminating experience will allow students to create a project that will facilitate their transition into a post baccalaureate environment.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: History and Philosophy of Biology
courses.description: Development of fundamental generalizations of biology; nature of science; applications to major philosophical issues of current science.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Biology Student Teaching
courses.description: Field-based, semester-long experience in teaching secondary students; demonstrating proficiency in all program standards.  Seminar (Sc Ed 490R) required.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Secondary Teaching Internship
courses.description: Culminating experience for students in the Biological Sciences Education major. Student participate in an internship teaching experience in a public school setting within one of the five BYU partnership districts. The internship requires students to complete a full school year of teaching in the assigned public school.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Field Exam and Exit Survey
courses.description: This course will allow students to reflect on the meaningful learning opportunities they have experienced at BYU, how those experiences have shaped their education, and what role experiential learning has played in their intellectual, professional, and spiritual development. This opportunity for broader reflection is a crucial culminating activity as students prepare for graduation. Students will be reminded of the importance of lifelong learning and will take the ETS Biology Major Field Exam. This national exam evaluates the students’ learning and retention of major scientific concepts in the fields of molecular biology, cell biology, organismal biology, population biology, and analytical skills.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Research Orientation
courses.description: Introduction to graduate school and research techniques.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Biological Systematics for Curation
courses.description: Principles, methods, and tools of taxonomy and systematics as applied to species delimitation, specimen-based research, nomenclatural codes with additional emphasis on curation of biological specimens.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Lichenology
courses.description: Classification, morphology, and ecology on lichens.  Field trip required.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Publishing in Peer-Reviewed Journals
courses.description: Each student enrolled in this course will be guided through the processes of writing a scientific manuscript and submitting it for publication in a peer-reviewed journal.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Symbiosis
courses.description: For graduate and upper-level undergraduate students, an introduction to the differences and commonalities among a diverse range of symbioses involving animals, plants, fungi and prokaryotes and the ways in which they influence biological communities. Topics include the human gut microbiome, mycorrhizas, plant-rhizobium symbiosis, plant-insect symbioses, marine invertebrate-bacterial symbioses, ant symbioses, lichens and soil crusts.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Science Communication
courses.description: Students will learn concepts, theory, philosophy, and practice of science communication.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Advanced Genetic Analysis
courses.description: Close examination of core genetic principles as presented in both classic and current literature with the goal of understanding current uses of genetics to examine gene function. Emphasis given to the experimental basis of transmission genetics (transfer of information between generations) as presented in classic studies and contemporary uses of genetic analysis to define gene function in current literature.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Aquatic Entomology
courses.description: Morphology, classification, biology, and functional ecology of aquatic insects. Field trips required.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Behavioral Ecology
courses.description: Students in Behavioral Ecology will study the biological mechanisms and evolutionary causes and consequences of a range of animal behaviors.  The course will be geared towards helping students to gain a broad perspective of the range of factors that influence animal behavior and to provide students with the tools conduct, evaluate, and understand research on the ecology of animal behavior.  We will cover a broad range of topics that are central to the field of behavioral ecology, including the economics of behavioral decisions, predator-prey arms races, resource competition, group living, reproductive selection and conflict, parental care, mating systems, social behaviors, cooperation and altruism, and communication.  Each of these topics will be examined from an evolutionary and ecological perspective, with a focus on helping students first to understand the underlying theory and concepts, and second to grasp the research techniques and approaches used to increase knowledge in this field.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Evolutionary and Ecological Modeling
courses.description: Using models in ecology.  Practical experience in analytical, simulation, and agent-based models.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Limnology: Inland Waters
courses.description: This course covers fundamental concepts and skills for studying lakes and their biota and physical/chemical properties.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Stream and Wetland Ecology
courses.description: Stream and wetland ecology; their biota and their physical/chemical properties.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Ecology and Evolution
courses.description: Current topics in ecology, evolution, and systematics.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Biological Science Education
courses.description: Topics include epistemology, pedagogy, innovative curriculum, and scientific education research.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Population Genetics
courses.description: Basic principles of population genetics applied to natural populations; drift, selection, and nonrandom mating; inferring population subdivision, migration, and gene flow.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Machine Learning for Biologists
courses.description: Students will learn concepts and applications of machine-learning techniques applied to diverse types of biological data.

courses.title: Ecology Science In-Service
courses.description: In-service course for science teachers.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Phylogenetic Systematics
courses.description: Theoretical foundations of modern systematics, methods of phylogenetic inference, and discussion of contemporary literature.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: (Bio - MMBio) Molecular Evolution.
courses.description: Theoretical foundations of molecular evolution; molecular phylogenetics, estimates of population genetic parameters, gene duplication, horizontal gene transfer, rates of evolution, molecular clocks.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Evolutionary Ecology
courses.description: Exploring the diversity of life by integrating ecological and evolutionary perspectives.  Topics include theoretical population ecology, advanced evolutionary biology, and behavioral ecology.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Community and Ecosystem Ecology
courses.description: Integrating ecological and biogeochemical concepts to understand the structuring of biological communities and ecological systems. Topics include community assembly, trophic dynamics, systems biology, ecosystem services, and biodiversity-ecosystem function.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Speciation and Phylogeography
courses.description: Students will understand theoretical foundations of speciation and phylogeography including key theories and research practices; implement empirical approaches to analyze, interpret, and communicate relevant biological issues; and conceive, execute, and present a related independent research study.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Bioinformatics and Data Analysis
courses.description: Bioinformatics skills have become critical for biological research. This course is intended to introduce students to bioinformatics. Students will be introduced to the Linux operating system and gain skills in employing it in research. They will also learn computer-programming skills using the Python language. Students will acquire the skills to perform data manipulations and simple analyses on biological datasets.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: R Programming Essentials
courses.description: Students will develop skills in using R programming and existing algorithms to analyze biological data and to critically analyze results. Students learn to write code in the R programming language, complete machine-learning tasks, and create data visualizations.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: University Teaching 1: Advanced Pedagogical Methods
courses.description: An exploration into learning theories that influence teaching pedagogies: understanding how students learn; designing curriculum to fit current research-backed models of learning; understanding assessment strategies; practicing backward design; and preparing graduate students for an authentic teaching experience.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: University Teaching 2: Instructional Design
courses.description: Guided experience in development and evaluation of instructional product: analyzing learning outcomes; developing instructional materials and assessment instruments; critique of finished instruction; and practical experience under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: University Teaching 3: Mentored Classroom Practicum
courses.description: Authentic teaching experience under the mentorship of a faculty member.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Science Education
courses.description: Current topics in biological science education.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Special Problems in Biology
courses.description: Independent student research under faculty supervision.

courses.subject: BIO
courses.title: Practicum in Biology Teaching
courses.description: Curricula, principles, concepts, and experiences in teaching biology effectively.

courses.description: Concentration on Burmese language and culture issues for specific careers.

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: How to Program
courses.description: Introduction to programming and computer science for those with no prior programming experience. Focuses on the basic aspects of programming, with an emphasis on core principles. Labs provide a supportive environment to learn how to program with peers. Weekly discussions will introduce some of the many ways computer science interacts with society. Programming assignments will demonstrate how to use computing in a variety of disciplines. \n
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.description: Teaches how to design, develop, reason about, and test programs. Topics include higher-order functions, object-oriented programming, recursion, algorithms, data structures, decomposition, interpreters, and regular expressions.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming
courses.description: Introduction to object-oriented program design and development.  Principles of algorithm formulation and implementation.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Data Science
courses.description: This course is a broad, interdisciplinary look at the field of data science, and how to derive insight from data.  It will develop technical skills (including some python programming, statistics, linear algebra, machine learning, data cleaning and visualization) as well as data literacy (mental frameworks for decomposing data science problems, critical thinking about potential conclusions of an analysis, and potential pitfalls of overreliance on unreliable data).
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Exploring Computer Science
courses.description: Introduction to the discipline of computer science and its fields. Lectures will provide an accessible introduction to the fields of computer science for those who are new to the discipline.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Academic Internship
courses.description: Internships or cooperative education experiences with organizations outside BYU.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Undergraduate level subjects as announced before each semester.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Software Engineering Lab 1
courses.description: The first of three experiential learning labs that will provide students with hands-on experience with various tools, technologies, and techniques that software engineers use in practice. In addition to hands-on lab experiences, this course contains lecture and assigned reading content that will provide an understanding of what a software engineering career is and what roles and responsibilities are available to software engineers.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Software Engineering Lab 2
courses.description: The second of three experiential learning labs that will provide students with hands-on experience with various tools, technologies, and techniques that software engineers use in practice. The lab experiences in this course build on those learned in CS 202 and focus on tools and techniques for source code testing, automated source code analysis, and source code build and dependency management.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Software Engineering Lab 3
courses.description: The third of three experiential learning labs that will provide students with hands-on experience with various tools, technologies, and techniques that software engineers use in practice. The lab experiences in this course build on those learned in CS 202 and CS 203 and focus on tools and techniques for cloud development and Agile programming.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Systems
courses.description: How a computer works to execute sequential code: low level data representation and abstraction, the relationship between C and assembly, computer architecture and pipelining, the memory hierarchy, dynamic memory allocation, and linking.\n
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Fundamental data structures and algorithms of computer science; basic algorithm analysis; recursion; sorting and searching; lists, stacks, queues, trees, hashing; object-oriented data abstraction.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Introduction to grammars and parsing; predicate and propositional logic; proof techniques; sets, functions, relations, relational data model; graphs and graph algorithms.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Advanced Software Construction
courses.description: Advanced software development with an object-oriented focus. Design, implementation, and testing of medium-sized programs including a server program.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Computational Theory
courses.description: Finite state automata, regular languages, lexical analysis; push-down automata, context-free languages, parsing; Turing machines and unrestricted grammars; computability complexity, NP-completeness.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Human Computer Interaction
courses.description: Design user experiences with technology that make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. Methods to establish user needs, derive designs, assess tradeoffs, and report results. Develop and iterate prototypes with feedback from representative users.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Web Programming
courses.description: Introduction to building and deploying full stack web applications using core technologies, frameworks, protocols, and development tools.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: Understand the fundamental models of machine learning, such as neural networks, decision trees, data mining, clustering, Bayesian learning, ensembles, reinforcement learning, and deep learning. Work with data and machine learning tools in real world applications.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Careers in Computer Science
courses.description: Career advising for students in computer science. Advice on resumes, applications, and interviews for internships, full-time jobs, and graduate school. Opportunities to network with other students and with employers.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Undergraduate-level topics as announced.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
courses.description: A study of the design and analysis of algorithms as solutions to problems, including dynamic programming, linear programming, greedy algorithms, divide-and-conquer algorithms, graph algorithms, and intelligent search algorithms.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Systems Programming
courses.description: Systems programming principles and concepts, including Linux systems programming, multiprocessing, concurrency, exceptional control flow, caching, sockets, protocols, and non-blocking I/O.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Quality Assurance and Developer Operations
courses.description: Comprehensive production software testing, deployment, and management strategies, focusing on automation, security, quality assurance, continuous integration/deployment, scalability, and resilience.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Concepts of Programming Languages
courses.description: Principles and concepts characterizing high-level computer programming languages, process and data abstration, encapsulation, inheritance, functional programming, logic programming, scanners, and parsers.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Software Design
courses.description: Use design, development, testing and refactoring techniques to build and evolve reliable, maintainable and scalable software systems. Covers a wide range of design patterns and principles. Also introduces students to software architecture and architectural patterns.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Operating Systems Design
courses.description: Principles and concepts of operating systems design and the implementation of an operating system.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Interactive Graphics and Image Processing
courses.description: Introduces basic concepts of computer graphics and image processing. Includes characteristics of physical cameras and displays; color models; basic image processing algorithms: 2D and 3D homogeneous coordinate transformations; fundamentals of 3D rendering geometry; lighting and shading: image warping and texture mapping; and frequency-domain processing.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences
courses.prerequisites_text: C S 240 or (C S 240 and MATH 213 and MATH 215)

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Advanced Techniques in Human Computer Interaction
courses.description: This class combines designing the user experience with implementing the technology. Students learn website design, information architecture, and how to design for the broader ecosystem of use. Finally, students will learn principles specifically relevant to website design and information architecture. Web design is one of the most common UX jobs and so this makes their skills highly marketable.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Collaborative Problem Solving
courses.description: Strengthen problem-solving skills through targeted practice to prepare for technical/coding interviews (a key challenge when job interviewing). Building on techniques from CS 312, learn to collaborate and quickly identify and apply appropriate strategies to problems.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Undergraduate level subjects as announced before each semester.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Ethics and Computers in Society
courses.description: Societal impact of computer technology, the computer scientist's place in society, ethical issues.  Reading, discussion, and writing seminar.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Creating and Managing a Software Business
courses.description: Entrepreneurship, idea/opportunity generation, strategic planning, legal organization, product development, marketing/sales, customer support, fund raising, and effective management.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Linear Programming and Convex Optimization
courses.description: Optimization, problem formulation, and solution algorithms, including simplex and interior point methods.  Applications from control, data mining, finance, game theory, learning, network flow, operations research, and statistical estimation.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Advanced Algorithms
courses.description: Advanced Algorithms and Problem Solving topics including combinatorics, prime number theory, network flow and matching, computational geometry, randomized algorithms, advanced dynamic programming, algorithms and data structures for strings, trees, graphs and sequences.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Bioinformatics Algorithms
courses.description: Students are introduced to bioinformatics algorithms, which are used to study diverse areas of biology. They gain experience implementing many of these algorithms and understand how these algorithms are leveraged to analyze biological datasets.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Analysis, design, implementation, and testing of significant software systems.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Formal Verification
courses.description:
Introduction to mathematical formalization and techniques to rigorously establish properties of data structures, functions, and whole programs, including imperative features. Students use a proof assistant embedding several languages including an advanced functional
language.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Algorithmic Languages and Compilers
courses.description: Formal description of algorithmic languages and techniques used in their compilation:  semantics, ambiguities, procedures, replication, iteration, recursion.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.description: Introduction to principles, algorithms, and techniques that allow computers to analyze images and video, including feature detection, image classification, object detection and recognition, segmentation, and 3D perception.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences
courses.prerequisites_text: C S 312 and MATH 213 and MATH 215

courses.description: Database models:  relational, deductive, object-oriented.  Integrity constraints, query languages, database design.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.description: Concepts and terminology of information retrieval (IR) systems.  Design methodologies and issues.  Fundamental IR models examined:  Boolean, Vector Space, Probabilistic models, and evaluation strategies.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S

courses.description: Interactive computer graphics systems programming and architecture.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Mobile and Ubiquitous Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Iterative user experience design for mobile and ubiquitous computing with an emphasis on conceptualization and prototyping in specific contexts. Complete an open-ended project from initial design through functional prototype, with design and critique sessions.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Computer Communications and Networking
courses.description: Introduction to data communications and computer networking.  Communications fundamentals, computer networks, software, architecture, telecommunications, regulation, standards.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Large-Scale Distributed System Design
courses.description: Principles and concepts of designing and building distributed systems.  Introduction to architectures for distributed computation.  Reliability, availability, and scalability of large applications.  Cloud computing and APIs.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Computer Security
courses.description: Provides a broad introduction to computer security. Topics include operating system security, software security, cryptography, authentication, web security, and threat modeling.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences
courses.prerequisites_text: (C S 224 and C S 260) or (EC EN 224 and C S 260)

courses.title: Blockchain Technologies
courses.description: Technical underpinnings of blockchain-based systems, including cryptocurrency, smart contracts, decentralized finance (De-Fi), and Web3. Explores which problems are suitable for a blockchain-based solution and discusses arguments in favor and against blockchain systems.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduction to core areas of artifical intelligence; intelligent agents, problem solving and search, knowledge-based systems and inference, planning, uncertainty, learning, and perception.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences
courses.prerequisites_text: (C S 312 and MATH 215 and STAT 121) or (C S 312 and MATH 215 and STAT 201) or (C S 312 and STAT 121)

courses.title: Voice User Interfaces
courses.description: Methods and development platforms for Voice User Interfaces. Principles of effective design; differences from visual or menu-based interfaces’ mechanics of automatic speech recognition, intent detection, slot filling, dialog state tracking, text generation, and knowledge representation.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Advanced Machine Learning
courses.description: Understand the fundamental models of machine learning, such as neural networks, decision trees, data mining, clustering, Bayesian learning, ensembles, reinforcement learning, and deep learning. Work with data and machine learning tools in real world applications.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: C S
courses.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
courses.description: Understand theory and practice of deep learning, drawing material from machine vision, machine translation, dynamical systems, audio processing, neural computing and human perception. Learn supporting mathematical concepts, including linear algebra, stochastic optimization, and hardware acceleration.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.title: Secondary Minor Student Teaching
courses.description: Supervised, full-day, four week experience to develop and demonstrate competence in teaching minor area course content in the secondary classroom.

courses.description: Evolution of machine translation technologies and algorithms, with a foundation in basic algorithms, human-machine interaction, automatic adaptation, statistical and neural models, multilingual models, multimodal models, quality evaluation and estimation, and speech-to-speech translation.

courses.description: Introduction for science, math, and statistics majors to careers in industry. Project planning, oral and written business presentations, business accounting, and technology readiness.

courses.description: Students will engage in guided clinical observations to learn practical clinical methods in the field of audiology and speech language pathology. courses.college: David O. McKay School of Education

Experiences will enhance student learning through hands-on activities and close collaboration with faculty or a qualified on-campus mentor.
courses.college: David O. McKay School of Education

Relevant research will also be reviewed and discussed.

Students will learn to use industry databases, media monitoring platforms, and open-source information to generate quality insights and developed strategies under tight client deadlines. The course emphasizes the need for new age application of tools and approaches that encourage speed, accuracy, and synthesis, preparing students to deliver actionable intelligence that supports client goals. In today’s industry, professionals are expected to make smart business decisions with tighter turnarounds while still maintaining excellence in quality.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Is entrepreneurship for you? Basics of entrepreneurship, its importance to society, opportunities to pursue a startup company, and impact on future careers.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Startup Bootcamp
courses.description: Learn and apply the basic skills to create a startup company. Work in teams to identify entrepreneurial opportunities and develop innovative solutions. Interact with real customers to validate business assumptions.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Fundamentals of Starting a Business
courses.description: Practical aspects of business formation and growth; create and launch a business and generate revenue under the guidance of course faculty.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Business Model Ideation & Validation
courses.description: Create a successful new venture by validating an initial idea and subsequent business model.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Legal Issues in Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Legal risks faced by entrepreneurs. How to plan for and avoid legal problems including forming the business, legal liability, and protecting assets.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Sales & Persuasion
courses.description: This course focuses on fundamentals of human persuasion and sales in the early stages of business (new ventures, startups, and growth companies). These include the skills practiced by accomplished salespeople to navigate the different steps of a sale, grounded in an understanding of purchase decisions. It also addresses persuasion in the context of raising capital, recruiting and motivating employees, and establishing partnerships. The importance of ethics and creativity throughout selling process are addressed as well.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Career Development and Student Mentoring
courses.description: Introduction to the resources, services, and opportunities for career development available to business management majors. Specific projects include developing a career plan, refining interviewing and networking skills, and interacting individually with a mentor well-established in a directly relevant career.\n

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Digital Marketing
courses.description: Digital marketing for entrepreneurs: acquire first customers using SEO, social media, email marketing, and online ads. Emphasizes strategies to build awareness, validate markets, improve conversion, and grow revenue for new ventures.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition
courses.description: Entrepreneurial acquisition of existing businesses. Identify, evaluate, and pursue opportunities through search, due diligence, negotiation, and financing. Includes franchising and development of a personalized acquisition strategy for business ownership.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Entrepreneurship Lecture Series
courses.description: Lectures about entrepreneurship by successful entrepreneurs.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Technology Entrepreneurship Lecture Series
courses.description: Lectures about technology entrepreneurship by successful entrepreneurs.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Innovation
courses.description: Finding and validating ideas for innovative new ventures with a focus on customer pain, elegant solutions, and markets.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Entrepreneurship Analytics
courses.description: Analysis of expected profitability of startups. Students collect and analyze data to find demand curves, cost curves, profit curves, optimal prices and competition in various competitive environments. Economic principles are used to make decisions about whether to launch new ventures.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Creating New Ventures
courses.description: Learning the critical skills to create a successful new venture by validating an initial idea and business model in the field.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Financing New Ventures
courses.description: Concepts and skills of entrepreneurship, emphasizing how new and emerging companies are financed. Applying functional tools to case situations.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Managing New Ventures and Family Business
courses.description: How to operate, grow, and exit new ventures and family-owned businesses following their creation and funding. Consulting project required.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Venture Capital for Startups
courses.description: Explore how successful startups navigate obtaining funding from venture capital firms, the typical terms and structures of those relationships, and how they manage those relationships over time. Considered from the perspective of both the venture capital firm and the founder seeking capital, with hands-on practice.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Building Your Lean Venture
courses.description: Explores the tasks entrepreneurs must master once they have settled on a business model and are ready to launch their business, including team building and leadership, product development, operations/logistics, financial modeling, fundraising, marketing, sales, client on-boarding and success.\n

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Innovation Practicum
courses.description: Theory and practice of innovation, emphasizing the discovery and development of innovative ideas in interdisciplinary teams.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Commercializing Innovation
courses.description: Commercializing innovations in interdisciplinary teams to bring innovative solutions to customers in the market.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: New Venture LaunchPad
courses.description: Student entrepreneurs currently building a business will learn business best practices through mentored learning with a proven entrepreneur. Topics covered include product-market fit, sales systems, pitches, boards, employees, compensation, leadership, ethics, and fundraising.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Experiential Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Introduction to entrepreneurial strategy principles, frameworks and tools; mentored on-campus internship with growth-stage company (OCI application required); preference given to entrepreneurial management majors.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Entrepreneurship Capstone
courses.description: Mentored consulting project to apply entrepreneurial management and innovation tools with a growth-stage company; preference given to entrepreneurial management majors.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Rapid Product Innovation & Development
courses.description: Processes, frameworks, and methods for validating ideas for innovative new products with a focus on understanding customer pain and needs, developing elegant solutions, and prototyping and testing those ideas.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Ideation & Team Formation
courses.description: Learn processes and methodologies to generate innovative business and product ideas across various industries and domains, and then determine the market opportunity and potential for ideas. In collaboration with teams, apply decision making frameworks to determine whether to pursue opportunities.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Software Product Management Lecture Series
courses.description: Lectures and networking with professionals and entrepreneurs involved in the development, launch, and growth of software products and businesses.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Venture Studio Practicum
courses.description: This student-led Venture Studio helps founders and operators of new ventures in their early stages to to begin and execute appropriate "next steps." This acceleration process is a beginning-to-end solution for new venture problems in tactical operations, sales and marketing, people organizations, legal and compliance, and engineering and product development as needed at each stage of the process. The course requires diligence, analysis, and resource application to reduce failure risk for new ventures by all key measures. Students will typically address client capability gaps in several market stages: Incubator/Accelerator; Studio; Bootstrap; and Angel/Seed stage.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Advanced Venture Studio
courses.description: An advanced course empowering student leaders through hands-on client work for entrepreneurs. This course goes further into identifying and acquiring critical resources for early companies. These resources include operations support, work space, and financial capital. Students provide clients state-of-the-art support functions in tactical operations, sales and marketing, people organizations, legal and compliance, and engineering and product development at various stages of business development.

courses.subject: ENT
courses.title: Topics in Entrepreneurial Management
courses.description: Special topics in entrepreneurship. Specific topics covered vary year to year.

courses.subject: ESL

courses.subject: ESL

courses.description: Improving the speaking ability of nonnative English students, emphasizing rhetorical and communication strategies, pronunciation, stress, rhythm, intonation, and fluency.

courses.subject: ESL

courses.subject: ESL

courses.subject: ESL
