courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experience Design
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles and practices of experience design. Students will explore how experiences shape identity, relationships and organizations. Students will learn to design experiences that matter in business, life, and Christlike discipleship.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Theories and Frameworks in Experience Design and Management
courses.description: An introduction to selected scientific theories, frameworks, and models that can be used to optimize experience design. An introduction to the experience economy and the design and management of experiences to create business value.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experience Design and Management Career Expeditions
courses.description: Field trips to exemplary experience design and management agencies. Opportunities to see experience design and management processes in action and connect with professionals in related career paths.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Risk Management in Experience Industries
courses.description: Overview of the legal process, legal issues, and risk management considerations regarding the jurisprudence to U.S. civil law as they relate to recreation experience industries.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experience-Centric Management
courses.description: An introduction to experience management beginning with an exploration of processes and principles for self- and team-management. Workflow and project management frameworks are discussed and analyzed for their compatibility with human-centered experience design and management.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experiential Marketing
courses.description: Marketing as a key aspect of the consumer experience along the entire customer journey. Creating impactful marketing materials during the pre-experience, designing engaging and last experiential marketing experiences, and effective follow-up strategies for post-experience. Introduction to strategic experiential marketing frameworks. Exposure to Adobe's Creative Suite.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Designing for Inclusion and Belonging
courses.description: In today’s world, designing for inclusion and belonging is not just a value—it’s a sacred responsibility rooted in the teachings of Jesus Christ. Students will increase awareness, question assumptions, and develop empathy-driven Christ-centered inclusion/belonging.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Designing for Inclusion and Belonging
courses.description: Focus on experiences of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging for individuals, families, and organizations. Address both the business and moral imperatives related to diversity, inclusion, and belonging.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experience Needfinding
courses.description: Skills to help organizations better understand end-user needs. Systematic collection and analysis of qualitative data through observations, interviews, and various other approaches. Utilizing  experience design to create innovative, data-driven solutions to create organizational value.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experience Insights
courses.description: Survey design and data analysis skills for data-informed decisions to demonstrate experience value. Analyses include descriptive statistics, bivariate relations and comparisons, and introduction to multiple regression. Data visualization and data storytelling.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Current Trends and Opportunities in the Experience Economy
courses.description: Explore current trends and entrepreneurship opportunities in the experiential segment of the consumer economy.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Guest, Visitor, and Customer Experience Management
courses.description: Focus on intentional customer experience management. How customer experience management can be a catalyst for organizations becoming more experience centric. Learn how to advocate for intentional customer experience management within organizations.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Emotional Intelligence for Experience Designers
courses.description: Emotional intelligence is key to becoming effective experience designers and managers. Utilize Deliberative Dialogues as a modality to help students develop and practice empathy, self-awareness, self-regulation, and social skills (specifically positive communication and civil discourse).

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Topics in Experience Design and Management
courses.description: Special topics, mentored research, and learning experiences, including attending professional conferences, Study Abroad participation, and other learning experiences.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experience Design and Management Lab
courses.description: Hands-on lab where you apply your acquired experience design and management knowledge, insights, tools, and skills to work on real projects for businesses in various industries. You will take on a project, meet with the organization to work through the discovery phase, then ideate, prototype, experiment, measure, and iterate to build an experience focused solution for their business challenge.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Professional Preparation in Experience Design and Management
courses.description: Focuses on developing the professional competencies of experience design students consistent with industry expectations. Examines professional career preparation including skills assessment, portfolio building and resume writing, internship application processes, interview techniques, college-to-career transition, professional ethics and selected contemporary career building seminar topics.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Senior Internship
courses.description: 300-hour internship in Experience Design & Management where students apply junior core coursework, build NACE career competencies, demonstrate ExDM skills, and gain experience in professionalism, career exploration, and articulating a personal professional story.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Experience Design Research Seminar
courses.description: Introduction to terms, methodologies, and research literature relevant to current experience design and management research. Also explores relevant graduate programs and academic careers.
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXDM
courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.department: Experience Design and Management, Department of

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Introduction to Exercise Sciences
courses.description: Provides new majors with an overview of the Exercise Sciences majors and department.  Includes a general review of the field of exercise science and specifically addresses expectations for course work and timelines (MAP review), details on similarities and differences between the undergraduate major options (Exercise Sciences and  Exercise and Wellness), introduction to the Master of Athletic Training program, and opportunities for internship and research. Also presents opportunities for introductions to EXSC faculty, career options and possibilities (presentations by practicing allied health professionals), college/university advisement and counseling resources, and post-graduate education options.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Science of Wellness
courses.description: A comprehensive study of the science of wellness of the whole individual. The science of wellness draws principles from exercise sciences, biological sciences, behavioral and social sciences. The research from psychoneuroimmunology (PNI) supports specifically the holistic wellness paradigm whose focus is that every aspect of each human being, the body, mind and spirit, are involved in all wellness activities and all wellness activities affect the whole individual. Students will discover this new paradigm and experience the blending of the sciences to support the integrated nature of our being.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Basic Athletic Training
courses.description: Recognition, evaluation, and care of athletic injuries. Techniques in taping, preventing, and rehabilitating injuries.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Basic Athletic Training Lab
courses.description: Lab with techniques in preventing the injured through taping, wrapping, bracing and padding, and for treating and transporting injuries by splinting, wrapping, using ambulatory aids and spine boarding.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Body, Mind, Spirit
courses.description: Sacredness of the body and its meaningfulness to the whole being. Comparative approach utilizing ideas from the restored gospel and Western and Eastern philosophy (nature of being).

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Research Methods and Evidence Based Practices
courses.description: This class will help students: 1) develop skills to access and evaluate scientific literature, 2) value the role of systematic investigation of diverse resources in personal and professional decision making, and 3) prepare to participate in meaningful mentored research with professors.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Exercise Is Medicine
courses.description:
This course introduces and provides evidence for the notion that physical activity promotes optimal physical, mental, and spiritual health and is integral in the prevention and treatment of many medical conditions. Students will read and discuss current literature supporting exercise as a powerful adjunct to modern medical treatment strategies. In-class experience will involve a
team-based learning approach, discussion of case studies, and practice learning and sharing with others the life-changing truth that exercise is indeed the best medicine.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Kinesiology and Biomechanics
courses.description: The influence of physical laws on human movement. Physical laws that will be discussed include linear and angular motion, force and torque, center of mass, fluid mechanics, and tissue mechanics.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Personal Training Strategies
courses.description: The art and science of personal fitness training for healthy adults, utilizing safe and effective techniques to develop and maintain optimal functional fitness (proper posture, balance, joint mobility, and stability), and optimal physical fitness (cardiorespiratory endurance, flexibility, muscular strength, and power).

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Lifestyle and Chronic Disease Prevention
courses.description: Current scientific evidence demonstrating how lifestyle affects disease processes. Healthy lifestyle concepts specifically needed by wellness professionals, health educators, and health promotion practitioners; influence of unhealthy lifestyle as basis for chronic diseases, i.e., cardiovascular disease, cancer, and diabetes.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Huntsman World Senior Games Internship
courses.description: On-the-job experience for Huntsman World Senior Games interns.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Exercise Sciences Internship
courses.description: EXSC 399R is an academic internship in which student learning is enhanced through practical work experiences supervised by a qualified professional mentor. Students will engage in an experiential learning framework of intention, integration, and reflection to identify and develop professional skills and competencies and apply them to future career or life plans.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Stress Management
courses.description: Teaches students the basic principles, theories, and relaxation techniques to effectively manage personal stress. Students gain a greater understanding of the mind-body relationship, learn to employ a holistic approach to stress, and adopt effective cognitive, coping, and relaxation techniques. Ultimately, students experience a more effective approach to optimal lifelong health.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Musculoskeletal Human Anatomy (includes lab)
courses.description: Advanced examination of structure and function of skeletal, articular, muscular, and peripheral nervous systems with clinical applications; cadaver lab included.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Worksite Health Promotion
courses.description: Managing, designing, marketing, implementing, assessing, and administering health promotion programs in a worksite setting.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Orthopaedic Impairments and Therapeutic Exercise
courses.description: Fundamentals of body mechanics and therapeutic exercise, coupled with kinesiological principles for detection and correction of basic neuromusculoskeletal anomalies.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Clinical Biomechanics
courses.description: Advanced biological and mechanical perspectives into the etiology, diagnosis, and therapeutic resolution of common musculoskeletal disorders.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Exercise Physiology
courses.description: The function of the physiological systems and their responses to acute and chronic exercise.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Exercise Physiology Lab
courses.description: Introduction of laboratory and field methods; applying principles of exercise physiology to assessing physical fitness and physiological responses to exercise.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Introduction to Electrocardiograms
courses.description: Cardiovascular physiology and conduction pathways of the heart. Resting and exercise 12-lead ECG preparation, recording and interpretation of normal ECG patterns, myocardial infarctions, and common atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. This course takes an approach to understanding ECGs applicable to students in exercise science-related fields of study and occupations, including the allied health or medical professions.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Exercise Prescription
courses.description: Applying knowledge of human physiology in developing appropriate exercise programs for individuals with a variety of needs and fitness levels; using the effects of exercise to improve health and quality of life.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Functional Neuroanatomy
courses.description: Function, assessment, and rehabilitation of sensory and motor systems.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Obesity and Weight Management
courses.description: Review of the scientific literature surrounding obesity and weight management, primarily the causes and consequences of this growing epidemic.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Exercise and Wellness Certification Preparation
courses.description: Review of exercise and wellness certification competencies and curriculum with preparation for professional certification.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Motor Control
courses.description: This upper level exercise sciences course will synthesize neuromuscular and biomechanical principles from other courses in the department (i.e., EXSC 362, 440 and 463) and introduce new physiological principles that direct healthy, purposeful control of voluntary movement. Course concepts will include (1) neuromuscular anatomy and physiology, (2) biomechanics of single- and multi-joint systems, (3) current questions and pressing problems related to healthy and pathological control of voluntary movement, (4) current approaches to improving athletic performance, and (5) overcoming orthopedic and neuromuscular impairments.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Undergraduate Research and Study
courses.description: Individual research and study in any area of exercise science.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Pathophysiology for the Athletic Trainer
courses.description: Foundational understanding of the physiology underlying common systemic diseases. Recognize, evaluate and differentiate common systemic diseases.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Athletic Training Lab
courses.description: Advanced athletic training skills, including taping, bracing and splinting, custom-fitted equipment, massage and stretching techniques, and emergency splinting and transport.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Therapeutic Interventions 1, Modalities
courses.description: Principles of therapeutic interventions: healing, hydrotherapy, massage, traction, radiant energy, heat, cold, electrotherapy and rehabilitation. Application of healing and therapeutic modality theories to injured athletes and physically active individuals.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Orthopedic Evaluation 1: Lower Extremities
courses.description: Advanced principles of lower-extremity injury evaluation; evaluation techniques for the lower extremities.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Orthopedic Evaluation 2: Upper Extremities and Trunk
courses.description: Advanced principles of injury evaluation; evaluation techniques for the upper extremities and trunk.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Therapeutic Interventions 2, Rehabilitation
courses.description: Knowledge in and application of rehabilitation theories with regards to therapeutic exercise for injured and uninjured physically active individuals.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Medical Issues in Athletic Training
courses.description: Discussion of current medical issues in athletic training with guest lectures by medical specialists from the community.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Environmental Physiology
courses.description: Study environmental stressors and physiological  responses (neuromuscular, cardiovascular, cellular energy metabolism) during exposure to  heat, cold, high altitude, hyperbaric diving, and zero-G.  Examine  how various physiological systems function during acute exposure to these environmental extremes.\n\n

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Pharmacology in Athletic Training
courses.description: Foundational concepts in pharmacology and pharmcological interventions for students in a variety of allied health professions. Specifically tailored to the Athletic Training master's student.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Graduate Athletic Training 1
courses.description: Review of the practice of athletic training, from professional organizations, legal and ethical foundations, care of injury ranging from emergencies to orthopedic evaluation and systemic pathology.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Graduate Athletic Training 2
courses.description: The practice of athletic training from professional and legal behavior to care of injury ranging from policies and procedures to orthopedic evaluation.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Clinical and Educational Administration
courses.description:
Administration and management practices and issues in athletics, athletic training,
medicine, and various education settings. Ethical, moral legal, communication, and
professional etiquette are core concepts discussed.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Neural Basis of Rehabilitation
courses.description: Facilitating the discussion and knowledge of neuromechanics associated with orthopedic injury and rehabilitation. Becoming familiar with research in the area of neuromechanics; critical evaluation of such.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Mechanical Spinal Impairment and Mobilization
courses.description: Study of human spinal motion and function in relation to manual therapy techniques used to restore spinal mechanics.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Clinical and Educational Administration
courses.description: Administration and management practices and issues in athletics, athletic training, medicine, and various education settings. Ethical, moral legal, communication, and professional etiquette are core concepts discussed.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Musculoskeletal and Vascular Imaging
courses.description: Students will gain an understanding of the use and purpose of ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging for research in Exercise Sciences and clinical practice settings (i.e., athletic training, sports medicine, rehabilitation).

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Electrotherapy, Ultrasound, and Diathermy
courses.description: The history, theory, evidence-based research and application of several therapeutic modalities used in athletic training, physical therapy, and occupational therapy. Topics include: deep heating modalities (ultrasound and diathermy); electrotherapy (TENS, IFC, NMES, PENS, HVPC, iontophoresis).

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
courses.description: Topics will be rotated and may include: electrotherapy, ultrasound, and diathermy; cryotherapy; orthotics; clinical and educational administration; functional testing and exercise; neural basis of rehabilitation; strength rehabilitation; joint mobilization and manual therapy; spinal manipulation and mobilization.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Joint Mobilization and Manual Therapy
courses.description: The history, theory, evidence-based research, and application of joint mobilization of the ankle, knee, hip, shoulder, elbow and wrist joints; and positional release therapy.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Strength Rehabilitation
courses.description: Overview of different strength rehabilitation methods (and their history); examining their theoretical background and actual practice. Enhancing skills of critically reviewing literature.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Research Methods in Exercise Sciences
courses.description: Understanding, designing, and conducting research, including analysis of data using common statistical techniques.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Evidence-Based Practice
courses.description: Focus on research, both from the clinical involvement or consumer and the researchers' perspectives. Developing a clinical question and finding supporting evidence is the key to better outcomes. Patient outcome measures will be learned, analyzed and practiced.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Physical Activity and Health
courses.description: Role of physical activity and fitness in the prevention and reversal of disease, including type 2 diabetes, heart disease, cancer, osteoporosis, etc., and in the promotion of health.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Athletic Training Clinical Education 1
courses.description: Laboratory and field experience. First of four Athletic Training specialization and clinical  experiences (internships).

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Athletic Training Clinical Education 2
courses.description: Laboratory and field experience. Second of four Athletic Training specialization and clinical expectations experiences (internships).

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Athletic Training Clinical Education 3
courses.description: Laboratory and field experience. Third of four Athletic Training specialization and clinical expectations experiences (internships).

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Athletic Training Clinical Education 4
courses.description: Laboratory and field experience. Fourth of four Athletic Training specialization and clinical expectations experiences (internships).  Prepares students to practice as certified athletic trainers.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Worksite Wellness
courses.description: Management for effectively designing, marketing, implementing, and administering health promotion programs.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Motion Analysis Techniques
courses.description: Analysis of human movement using 2D and 3D kinematic and kinetic descriptions and models of motion based on 3D video and force plate techniques.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Neuromechanical Signal Collection and Processing
courses.description: Focus will be given to processing and interpretation of neuromechanical data, with an emphasis on electromyography and ground reaction force data.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Biomechanical Modeling
courses.description: Learn to use advanced biomechanics software to model, analyze, and interpret human movement. Create models of the human skeleton from motion capture data, represent motion in three dimensions using Euler angles, and perform inverse dynamics.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Computer Programming for Kinesiology
courses.description: Course designed to teach students to manage the large amounts of data collected during various analyses of human movement through computer programming. Students will also learn how to create their own software for data analysis.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Exercise Physiology
courses.description: Adjustments made by the body to accommodate physical activity.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Laboratory Methods and Procedures
courses.description: Basic techniques and procedures used in human performance laboratories.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Orthopaedic Anatomy
courses.description: Advanced regional musculoskeletal anatomy. Students dissect cadavers.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Lifestyle and Chronic Disease Prevention
courses.description: Managing health risks, particularly those relating to cardiovascular disease, cancer, and obesity.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Obesity and Weight Management
courses.description: Etiology, treatment, and prevention of obesity in various populations, emphasizing the role of exercise in weight control programs.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Health Promotion Practicum
courses.description: Field experience for health promotion graduate students (required); 50 hours of service in approved organization required per credit hour. Graduate students in other emphases may take this class with instructor's consent.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Athletic Training Internship
courses.description: Additional credit hours or fifth semester for athletic training clinical education experience or immersive internship experience for MAT students.  Each credit of internship will require 160 hours of work.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Orientation to graduate work in the exercise sciences.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Readings Seminar
courses.description: Searching, critiquing, and interpreting scientific literature with goal of conducting scientific research.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Athletic Training Capstone
courses.description: Synthesizing and integrating classroom and clinical experiences in preparation for BOC exam resulting in certification of athletic training students.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.description: Students demonstrate significant oral and written communication skills and research competencies through conceiving, proposing, and defending a thesis.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Doctoral Seminar: Professional and Scholarly Writing
courses.description: This class is designed to teach PhD students the essentials of writing good biomedical manuscripts for publication in appropriate scientific journals.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Doctoral Seminar: Research and Grantsmanship
courses.description: This class is designed to teach PhD students how to develop a research grant proposal focusing on appropriate structure and scientific content.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Exercise Physiology: Cardiopulmonary
courses.description: Cardiovascular and pulmonary physiology, assessments, responses to exercise, and interventions.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Advanced Exercise Physiology: Skeletal Muscle
courses.description: Effects of acute and chronic exercise on anatomy, physiology, and biochemistry of skeletal muscle.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Individual Research and Study in Exercise Sciences
courses.description: Individual research mentored by Exercise Sciences faculty. Number of credits is based on hours worked per week under contract.

courses.subject: EXSC
courses.title: Doctoral Dissertation
courses.description: Students demonstrate significant oral and written communication skills and research competencies through conceiving, proposing, and defending a dissertation.

courses.subject: FHSS
courses.title: Introduction to Civic Engagement Leadership
courses.description: Introduction to community involvement, public service, and leadership through lectures from external speakers and discussion of civic engagement.

courses.subject: FHSS
courses.title: FHSS Research Academy Seminar
courses.description: This course is part of the FHSS research academy and will help students build connections with other under-represented students, identify faculty and professional mentors, and prepare for graduate school by building skills that will help with tasks such as studying for graduate entrance exams, writing letters of intent, preparing resumes and CVs, and presenting.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: FHSS
courses.title: FHSS Career and Leadership Academy
courses.description: Explore your personality traits, skills, and career interests and prepare to make sound career choices, build connections with BYU alumni, improve your career efficacy, and prepare for your career pursuits after graduation.

courses.department: Family, Home, and Social Sciences, College of

The course also teaches students critical skills of analysis, evaluation, leadership, innovation, and teamwork by requiring the design and completion of a group project involving some form of civic improvement and incorporating interaction with an external community partner.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: FHSS
courses.title: Faith, Cultural Renewal, and Leadership Seminar
courses.description: Introduction to the major figures, events, and locations of Civil Rights Movements, with a focus on faith, courage, culture, and leadership.

courses.subject: FHSS
courses.title: Internship in Civic Engagement
courses.description: This course helps students engage in a series of experiences, while on their internship, that allow them to develop and demonstrate understanding of key competencies in professional contexts. Students will learn how to harness intention,  reflection, and integration of new learning to translate the value of their internship into a compelling, evidence-based narrative, tailored to an audience’s needs and expectations.

courses.title: Civic Engagement Leadership
courses.description: Promote leadership in civic engagement through discussion of community involvement and public service, lectures from external speakers, and development of a hands-on project involving some form of public service.

courses.description: Survival-level conversation, reading, listening, and culture skills in Fijian.

courses.title: First-Year Language Study: Fijian
courses.description: Beginning speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills in Fijian.

courses.subject: FIJI
courses.title: Advanced Language Proficiency Through Cultural Studies: Fijian
courses.description: Study of Fijian culture using interpersonal, presentational, and interpretive skills in the target language.

courses.subject: FIJI
courses.title: Introduction to Literature: Fijian
courses.description: Explore Fijian culture through stories, music, and history. Develop advanced proficiency using authentic materials, including film, literature, and other creative works.

courses.subject: FIJI
courses.title: Advanced Language Study for Career Purposes: Fijian
courses.description: Concentration on Fijian language and culture issues for specific careers.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Finance Recruitment Preparation
courses.description: Preparation for students interested in pursuing internships and jobs in finance.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Personal Finance
courses.description: Practical course in money management and utilizing savings.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Principles of Finance
courses.description: Financial management from the viewpoint of the business manager emphasizing profitability, liquidity, and long-range financial planning.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Investment Banking Recruiting
courses.description: Sophomore level class focused on preparing for the upcoming investment banking recruiting cycle. Corporate finance and accounting relevant for recruiting, formation of behavioral skills in a professional setting, and economic and banking landscapes.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Investments Academy
courses.description: Applying financial principles to practical investment problems and current events; understanding financial institutions, markets and their functions; insights into financial services and Wall Street professions.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Brigham Capital
courses.description: Team management of actual investment portfolio. Responsibility for identifying potential investments, modeling their financial value, and recommending portfolio actions.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Professional Development for Finance
courses.description: Student development and preparation for careers in finance. Recruiting resources, services, and career development opportunities. Developing a career plan, refining interviewing and networking skills, and interacting individually with mentors and professionals.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Analytical Methods in Finance
courses.description: Data description, visualization, and analysis, as applied to financial problems. Focus on developing perspectives on reasoning and decision making under uncertainty with application to real-world economic and financial issues. Quantitative methods for finance.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Advanced Financial Management
courses.description: Capital budgeting, cost of capital, capital structure/dividends, mergers and acquisitions, and current financial problems.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Managerial Finance for Non-Finance Majors
courses.description: Overview of financial management issues including capital budgeting, cost of capital, capital structure/dividends, and long-term financial planning.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Equity Financial Modeling and Valuation
courses.description: \tHands-on opportunity to work with security markets and perform security analysis. Builds on theory of investment development in Fin 410.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Investments
courses.description: Security markets, security analysis, and portfolio management.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Financial Derivatives
courses.description: Current investment literature, efficient markets, modern portfolio theory, capital assets pricing, options pricing theory with a focus on derivatives and fixed income strategies.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Real Estate Finance and Investment
courses.description: Terminology, concepts, principles, and analytical techniques related to financing of and investment in real estate.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Real Estate Development
courses.description: Applying financial and real estate principles to practical property investments; insights into the real estate profession.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Silver Fund
courses.description: Team management of actual investment portfolio. Responsibility for identifying potential investments, modeling their financial value, and recommending portfolio actions.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Real Estate Capital Markets & Investment
courses.description: Real estate capital markets, asset classes, investments, gateway, secondary and tertiary markets, demand drivers, deal structure, and transaction processes. Intuition development for early stage real estate career.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Financial Planning
courses.description: Apply financial principles to household decision making, stressing integration between areas. Income tax and estate planning, retirement, investments, portfolio management, and risk management.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Fixed Income Asset Management, Structured Products, and Risk
courses.description: Bonds as fundamental instruments of markets determining interest rates, including the wide array of instruments that are derivatives of bonds, rates, currencies, structured products and credit. Equilibrium pricing, arbitrage pricing, and financial engineering.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Capital and Security Markets
courses.description: How investors, market frictions, and financial institutions affect security prices, compensation for risk, and return patterns in capital and security markets. An analytical framework and quantitative tools to better analyze and understand capital markets.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Private Equity and Venture Capital
courses.description: Introduction to the private equity (PE) and venture capital markets, focusing almost exclusively on the American setting for these markets. Students will learn how PE and VC markets function, how PE and VC companies source their deals, and the valuation and forecasting models they use to make decisions. Exposure to examples of real-life transactions executed by PE and VC firms.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Mergers and Acquisitions, Restructuring, and Bankruptcy
courses.description: Fundamental skills in evaluating M&A and restructuring opportunities, including financial distress and bankruptcy. Practical modeling skills as well as the economic factors that drive value creation or destruction in restructuring situations.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: International Finance
courses.description: Investor and corporate financial decision making in international financial markets. Financial aspects of multinational corporations. Foreign exchange markets including pricing, exchange rate regimes, government intervention and hedging. International debt and equity financing.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Python and Finance
courses.description: Python tools for analyzing financial problems. Thinking programatically. Coding and financial applications.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
courses.description: Analysis of corporate financial statements emphasizing how accounting and managerial decisions shape reported results. Develop skills to evaluate earnings quality, assess financial risk, and build forward-looking financial projections to inform strategic business and investment decisions.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Fintech
courses.description: An exploration of technological innovations in financial services. Fintech economics and strategies, innovations in payments, and analytical tools to work with large data sets. Includes guest lectures from local fintech experts.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Trading and Market Structure
courses.description: Lectures and trading simulations to demonstrate how assets are traded. Trading orders, limit order books, liquidity, market manipulation, asymmetric information, algorithmic trading, high frequency trading, optimal trade placement.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Decentralized Finance
courses.description: Financial infrastructure built on blockchain networks. Digital signatures, consensus mechanisms, smart contracts, cryptocurrencies and architecture, decentralized exchange, lending protocols, decentralized derivatives, and asset tokenization.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Money, Banking, and Business
courses.description: Economic analysis of effects of money, banking, and financial institutions on business decisions and aggregate economic activity.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Finance Society Leadership
courses.description: Training for finance society association leadership. Includes active collaboration, working with professionals, faculty advisors and other students.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Capital Markets Academy
courses.description: Teams work on live, market-sensitive projects for financial services, including private equity, private wealth, insurance companies, and asset management.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Topics in Finance
courses.description: Current finance-related topics varying by semester and section.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: CFA Preparation
courses.description: Preparation to take Level I of the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) Exam. Topics covered on the exam, and with which students will be able to demonstrate strong proficiency, include: corporate finance, economics, financial reporting and analysis, quantitative methods, alternative investments, derivatives, equity investments, fixed income, and portfolio management and wealth planning.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Business Finance
courses.description: Short-term financing of a business operation.  Developing techniques for financial planning, such as analysis of ratios, profitability, and liquidity.

courses.subject: FIN
courses.title: Pre-PhD Finance Seminar
courses.description: Introduction to asset pricing theory using both analytical and numerical methods. Coverage includes the Capital Asset Pricing Model and Stochastic Discount Factor models. The empirical method of Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) is also introduced.

courses.subject: FNART

courses.description: Introduction to the integration of arts in education. Per Utah State Board of Education guidelines for the Arts Integration Endorsement, this course will give students training in implementation of Arts Integration in the classroom as well as in leadership and advocacy for the integration of arts in education.
courses.college: College of Fine Arts and Communications

courses.subject: FNART

courses.college: College of Fine Arts and Communications

courses.subject: FNART

courses.description: Taught in collaboration with the Rollins Center for Entrepreneurship and Technology. Application of foundational principles of entrepreneurship in developing goals as artists, performers, and creative professionals. The latest in design thinking, innovation, entrepreneurship, and the correct principles for starting or developing a business specifically related to the arts.\n
courses.college: College of Fine Arts and Communications

courses.subject: FNART
courses.title: Creativity and Collaboration in the Arts and Communications
courses.description: Explore theories of creativity, collaboration, and innovation in a modern, arts-based mediated world; engage in principles of team-building and communication; practice skills of ideation, research, and execution of interdisciplinary projects from conception to completion. Classes are project-based and vary from semester to semester. Please contact the College of Fine Arts and Communications (A-501 HFAC, 801-422-2819).
courses.college: College of Fine Arts and Communications

Students will read from a variety of text types in order to learn a range of linguistic structures and vocabulary, and become familiar with essential verbs and common syntax.

courses.subject: FREN

courses.subject: FREN

courses.description: Analysis of the contributions of women in French and/or Francophone literature. Assessment of the representations of women in French literary texts.

courses.description: Register for this course in consultation with department internship coordinator.  To be taken only when enrolled directly in French university as part of BYU professional program in France.  Only enroll when curriculum of other BYU courses do not correspond to the course enrolled in French university.

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Social Impact: Do Good Better
courses.description: Focuses on the most prominent approaches used in social impact and social innovation. Students develop skills in analyzing social ventures, including theory of change, solution evaluation, and social impact measurement; and leave with the confidence to pursue a life of purpose.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Designing Social Impact
courses.description: Use human-centered design to address social issues. Learn techniques focused on empathizing with the beneficiaries of the innovation, defining the beneficiaries' needs, ideating to create innovative solutions, prototyping creative solutions, and testing those solutions.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Implementing Social Impact
courses.description: Learn the advantages and disadvantages of intervention options in the four sectors (public, nonprofit, for-profit, civil society) and hybrid designs (collaboration, contracting, partnership). Learn how to fund and organize initiatives within the four sector framework.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Evaluating Social Impact
courses.description: Introduce theory and practice of social impact measurement. Examine need for social impact measurement, identify several competing contemporary approaches to social impact measurement, and compare and contrast the methods and effectiveness of different approaches.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Social Impact Lecture Series
courses.description: Lecture by successful social entrepreneurs and employees of high-impact social ventures significant to social impact.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Social Impact Projects
courses.description: Direct, practical on-campus and off-campus experience interning and consulting with established and recognized social innovators. Students apply to be involved in specific projects and are accepted to work on specific projects based on their skills.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Ballard Brief
courses.description: Write a Ballard Brief intended for publication. The Ballard Brief should reflect deep research and excellent writing on a social impact topic of wide concern to inform the general public on key issues and interventions.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: GoodMeasure
courses.description: GoodMeasure focuses on the practice of social impact measurement. Students use data to manage, evaluate, and achieve the desired program outcomes through faculty-supported semi-professional consultancies with government, business, and nonprofit organizations.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Startups for Good
courses.description: Explore the creation of businesses designed to address social issues. Through analysis, research, and mentoring, learn how startups for good operate and the unique challenges they encounter.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Corporate Social Impact
courses.description: Introduction to corporate led efforts in social impact. Shareholder, management, and employee views of corporate social impact (CSI) efforts. Frameworks for understanding increasing efforts by corporations to show demonstrable outcomes of their CSI efforts.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Impact Investing
courses.description: Impact investing markets, analysis, due diligence, and practice.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Advanced Impact Investing
courses.description: Advanced focus of impact investing due diligence and analysis methods. Practical application of these skills on current impact investment opportunities.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Creating Virtuous Organizations
courses.description: Identify the cornerstones of theory on which market systems are built, identify principles and practices for virtuous business, and connect with businesses and other organizations to refine, teach, and apply these principles and practices.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Advanced Social Impact
courses.description: Focuses on the study of high-impact social benefit organizations in nonprofit, governmental, church, education, for-profit, and hybrid environments. Advanced focus on using measurement and evaluation metrics to support long term project funding.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Improving Helping Behavior
courses.description: This class focuses on improving the ways you can be helpful to others, with a focus on informal helping. The course draws on research and evidence-based practices that lead to more effective helping behavior.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: GCI
courses.title: Topics In Social Impact
courses.description: Current social impact-related topics varying by semester and section.
courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.description: This course gives an overview of the discipline of geography and introduces students to the faculty and the geography major at BYU. In addition, the course helps students understand and prepare for future career and academic opportunities in their chosen field.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Global Environment: Understanding Physical Geography
courses.description: Physical environment, distribution and interrelationships of climates, landforms, ecosystems and their human significance.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Landscapes of Disaster:  An Introduction to Natural Hazards
courses.description: Exploring natural and social science of disturbances by analyzing causes, consequences, and role of human behavior in causing and mitigating natural disasters.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Geography and World Affairs
courses.description: Survey of the world, stressing geography of major political regions.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to Human Geography
courses.description: Culture distributions and their relationship to existing geographic phenomena.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to Urban and Regional Planning
courses.description: Introduction to the profession and practice of urban and regional planning.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Mapping Your World
courses.description: Managing and portraying geospatial information to solve geographic tasks using maps (cartography), aerial and satellite imagery (remote sensing), location services (GPS), and quantitative methods.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Concepts in the use of small- and large-scale digital map data, emphasizing landscape interpretation and feature description.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Programming for Geographers I
courses.description: An introduction to programming using appropriate modern programming languages for solving spatial problems
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Statistics for Geographers 1
courses.description: Methodology of spatial analysis.  Theory and techniques in geographic data description and population inference.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Geography of Utah
courses.description: Exploring geography of Utah.  Topics include land forms, climate, agricultural and recreational economics, historical migration, Mormon cultural landscape, ethnic patterns, and rural-urban contrasts.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: United States and Canada
courses.description: Analysis of the natural environment, historical development, cultural patterns, economic systems, and political structures of geographic regions.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Middle and South America
courses.description: Environmental, cultural, economic, and political parameters of Latin American societies.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Europe
courses.description: Systematic approach to physical base, social and political problems, economic issues, and regional summary.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Russia and the Former Soviet Union
courses.description: Physical features, resources, political issues, economy and industries, population concerns, and role in world affairs.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Middle East
courses.description: Physical and cultural geography of Southwest Asia and North Africa, emphasizing the cultural mosaic, geopolitics, environment, and resources of the region.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: East Asia
courses.description: Region of monsoon Asia and its basic human (demographics, nations and ethnic groups, settlement patterns, religious beliefs, transportation and communication systems, political structures), and physical geographic characteristics (land forms, physiography, climatic characteristics, and natural resources).
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Southeast Asia
courses.description: Fundamental issues of geography relating to Southeast Asia, including the extraction and marketing of natural resources, economic development, neighborly relations, and how diffusion has influenced the unique cultural, religious, and linguistic characteristics of the region.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: The Pacific Islands
courses.description: An examination of the physical, ecological and human environments of the Pacific islands, including the impacts of colonialism, warfare and military weapons testing, poverty, tourism, and environmental change in the region.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Africa South of the Sahara
courses.description: Geographical analysis focusing on resource management, political issues, development, environmental problems, economic development, and urban-rural change; case studies from selected countries.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Biogeography
courses.description: Broad-scale distribution of plants and animals.  Theoretical and practical applications to conservation and effects of global environmental change.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Climate and Society
courses.description: Temporal and spatial examination of the distribution, condition, and forecasting of different climatic characteristics across Earth. Effects of climate on society in the past, present and future, with a particular focus on the world’s most vulnerable populations.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Geography of Landforms
courses.description: Elements of landforms:  distributions and cultural significance.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Public Lands: Planning & Management
courses.description: Environmental and social geography of global protective land use designations: National Parks, Wilderness, Conservation areas, etc. Experience in building stakeholder collaborations to develop management plans.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Spatial Analysis of Environmental Data
courses.description: Introduction to a suite of quantitative spatial and spatio-temporal analysis tools, including landscape metric and fractal analysis, trend surface analysis, cluster analysis, analysis of scales of variation, geostatistics, point-to-point regression, and wavelet analysis.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Intermediate Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Collecting, managing, and analyzing spatial data to solve common geographic tasks.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Cartographic Design
courses.description: Graphic perception, layout, typography, color, statistical methods, and symbolization of thematic maps through computer-aided techniques.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Remote Sensing 1
courses.description: Introduction to airborne and spaceborne sensors, including characteristics and image acquisition.  Emphasizes land cover mapping applications appropriate for environment monitoring.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: GEOG

courses.description: GES 200 is the introductory class for the Global Environmental Studies minor and will prepare students for a broadly interdisciplinary engagement with environmental issues and challenges with an intercultural perspective. The class is managed by the program director with guest lecturers from among the Global Environmental Studies affiliated faculty highlighting different methodological and disciplinary approaches to ecological concerns. The specific issues and topics covered by the class will vary by semester, but every iteration will encompass the doctrinal foundations of environmental stewardship in the interdisciplinary context of the natural sciences, social sciences, arts, and humanities.

courses.subject: GES

courses.description: This course catalyzes learning about complex environmental challenges through research and service. As the capstone experience for the GES program, students will produce a research project and portfolio demonstrating mastery of the quantitative and aesthetic components of science and communication. The course consists of two major projects: 1) Assembling a portfolio of previous work demonstrating mastery of the GES program outcomes. 2) Identifying and carrying out a meaningful environmental research and service project addressing a pressing issue. Depending on the selected issue, this project may result in a peer-reviewed publication, a collaborative service project, or another outcome appropriate to the project. \n

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: (WS-Soc) Introduction to Global Women's Studies
courses.description: An introduction to the most important issues affecting women's lives and to contributions made by women both nationally and internationally.  The course will include historical, sociological, psychological, theological, legal, and/or cultural, and other approaches.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Women in the Scriptures
courses.description: A close examination of stories and writings about women found within the scriptural canon of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, focusing on the contributions of biblical women to the life, culture, religion, and history of Israel and the interpretation of their stories over time.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: The History of Latter-day Saint Women
courses.description: The religious, domestic, economic, political, social and familial lives of Latter-day Saint women within the broader contexts of American and global women's history and Latter-day Saint history. Mormon women's relationship to national trends and their association with national women's organizations.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Latter-day Saint Women as Cultural Producers
courses.description: Topics related to the ways Latter-day Saint women (historically and currently) have made cultural contributions, including an exploration of the significance of those contributions.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Women and Global Migration
courses.description: Exploration of how gender affects im/migration trends, laws, policies, patterns, and migrants' lived experiences, especially for women, and how migration occurs on a voluntary and involuntary basis between, within, and across borders. An examination of the role of sovereignty, liberalism, and citizenship in facilitating  or limiting -- the mass movement of women, their families, and communities.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Medieval European Women Writers
courses.description: Readings in European literature by women in the Middle Ages (prior to 1500).

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Early Modern European Women Writers
courses.description: Readings in European literature by women prior to 1700.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Modern European Women Writers
courses.description: Readings in European literature by women after 1700.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Pan American Women Writers
courses.description: Readings in literature by women from throughout the Americas from 1600 to the present, with a particular focus on the intersections of gender, race, class, ethnicity, and age.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: The Gendered Camera: Women and World Cinema
courses.description: Readings and practice in visual literacy and film theory related to women. A focus on the history of women in film with special attention to the work of early women film pioneers and women's world cinema from its beginnings to today.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Women Who Have Made a Difference
courses.description: This course focuses on a woman or a small group of women who have made important contributions in their fields, within their cultures, and/or to society locally or globally.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Women in Science
courses.description: Women scientists, their challenges, and their contributions to scientific knowledge in many fields.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women's Studies Special Topics
courses.description: Subjects related to women's studies and gender issues from a variety of disciplines.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women's Studies Colloquium
courses.description: Scholarly findings presented by researchers on topics relating to the effect of gender norms on the ways we live, the impact of social issues and power structures on women's lives, and the contributions of women throughout history and around the world.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: GWS Topics taught in Languages other than English
courses.description: The topics in this course relate to women and gender in non-English speaking cultures and communities. The course materials and instruction are offered in a language other than English.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women's Studies Mentored Study Experience
courses.description: Readings, research, and writing about women's lived experiences and contributions mentored by a faculty advisor. Intended for students enrolled in a study abroad program or a travel experience off campus, or for a student involved in a mentored research project with a faculty advisor.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women's Studies: Editing for Publication
courses.description: Students will gain experience copy editing by working on AWE: A Woman's Experience, the student journal for the Global Women's Studies program. Students will work as a team and with a faculty mentor to publicize, edit, design, and publish the latest issue of the journal.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women’s Studies Study Abroad Experience
courses.description: This course will focus on women’s contributions and women’s experiences on the global stage.  Course content will be tailored to incorporate the materials and learning opportunities found in the location(s) selected for the Study Abroad program (subject to change annually).

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women's Studies Internship
courses.description: Credit for work relating to issues affecting women's lives at an international, national, or local non-profit organization, business, or institution. Students will submit a written report of their internship experience.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women's Studies Theory
courses.description: International historical and contemporary theories and analysis of gender inequality from a variety of fields, including anthropology, sociology, communication, psychology, philosophy, literature, and education.

courses.subject: GWS
courses.title: Global Women's Studies Capstone
courses.description: Mentored research related to women or gender and leading to a senior capstone project and presentation.

courses.subject: HCOLL
courses.title: Humanities in Professional Life
courses.description: This course helps students frame their humanities experience as professional preparation. Students will learn how to translate the unique value of their degree as they pursue a variety of professional paths. In short, this class will explore what a Humanities graduate can do and why humanistic study meets so many needs in the modern workplace. By focusing on core professional competencies, students will find ways to make their major coursework relevant to life after graduation.

courses.subject: HCOLL
courses.title: Professional Internship Preparation
courses.description: Preparation to make an internship a professionally relevant experience. Professional competencies employers value most and how to develop them throughout the internship. Focus on professional competencies and the internship to identify ways to take initiative, add value, and successfully position for next steps in a career.

courses.subject: HCOLL
courses.title: Professional Internship
courses.description: This course helps students initiate a series of professional experiences, while on their internship, that allow them to develop and demonstrate understanding of key competencies in professional contexts. Students will learn how to harness intention, feedback, reflection, and integration of new learning to translate the value of the professional competencies into a powerful, evidence-based story of what they offer future employers.

courses.subject: HCOLL
courses.title: Humanities Research Seminar
courses.description: Research, writing, and discussion exploring enduring questions from perspectives offered by humanities disciplines.

courses.subject: HCOLL
courses.title: Humanities Lecture Series
courses.description: Lecture and discussion by scholars in the humanities, with supplementary reading and writing.

courses.subject: HCOLL
courses.title: Humanities On-campus Experiential Projects
courses.description: Practical, on-campus (not in the field) projects in which education is directly applied to real-world solutions for companies and other organizations. Students apply and are accepted to work on specific projects based on their skills, interests, and major emphasis.

courses.subject: HIST

courses.description: History within the broader framework of liberal education; nature of history; questions historians ask; skills and resources needed to study, understand, and write history.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: World Civilization to 1500
courses.description: World civilization from Greek antiquity to Renaissance; explores fundamental questions in the human experience, examines formative events in history, and seeks to teach value of important texts.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: World Civilization from 1500
courses.description: World civilization from Renaissance to present; explores fundamental questions in the human experience, examines formative events in history, and seeks to teach value of important texts.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Family History Doctrine and Practice
courses.description: Introduces basic genealogy and family history doctrine and genealogical methodology, emphasizing living memory, preservation, FamilySearch Family Tree, software, and citation.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Regional and Thematic Studies in Family History
courses.description: Exploration of sound genealogy/family history research methods and genealogical resources available for specified regions, countries, ethnicities, and/or language groups.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Family Historian's Craft
courses.description: Introduction to genealogical methods applicable in American and international research. Discussion of technology in genealogical research and introduction to censuses and vital records (US and international).
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Family and the Law in American History
courses.description: The interaction of families with law and government as illustrated in original American sources; individual family histories reconstructed in the broader perspective of history.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The United States Through 1877
courses.description: Discovery, colonization, American Revolution, estabishment of the Constitution, foreign affairs, westward expansion, slavery, sectionalism, Civil War, and reconstruction.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The United States Since 1877
courses.description: Industrialization, immigration, urbanization, political and social movements, and foreign policy.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to East Asian History
courses.description: Major themes in the history, thought, and culture of Asian societies from antiquity to the present.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST

courses.description: Survey of major developments in Christianity from its origins in the ancient Roman Empire to its global presence today.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST

courses.subject: HIST

courses.description: Cultures and empires of the Near East (Persia, Hellenistic kingdoms, Judaism, early Christianity, Rome, and Byzantium) from Alexander the Great to the Arab conquests.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST

courses.description: History of the Middle East in the modern period form 1800; rise of nation states, relationship with West, role of Islam.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: (Hist-NES 347R) Arab and Islamic Civilization.
courses.description: Social science/humanities core course covering Arab and Islamic civilization; historical evolution of Middle East to present. Overview of modern Palestinian society.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: (Hist-NES 349R) Jewish Civilization.
courses.description: Social science/humanities core course; broad introduction to Jewish self-understanding and history, focusing on relationships among people, faith, and land.

courses.subject: HIST

courses.description: Jewish diaspora, Jewish life in Europe; Yiddish culture; development of Zionism; emergence of modern Israel; Jewish-Christian relations; Jewish contributions to culture and society in the United States.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.title: German Family History Research and Methodology

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Eastern European Family History Research and Methodology
courses.description: Records, geographical-historical background, paleography, and methodologies for reconstruction of individual families; development of family history studies Eastern Europe.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Women in a Changing World

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Age of the French Revolution

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.title: African American Family History Research and Methodology
courses.description: Hist 296 is a research-intensive course introducing students to research methods, historical records, and challenges inherent to studying and writing African American family history.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of the Mediterranean Sea
courses.description: Explores the historiography and political, cultural, economic, and social history of the Mediterranean in the early modern period.

courses.subject: HIST

courses.description: A broad study of the many interconnected components of the healthcare industry, including medical technology, pharmaceuticals, hospital administration, healthcare policy, insurance, public health, etc. Introductory applications of various functional skills to healthcare.

courses.subject: HL
courses.title: Healthcare Leadership Lecture Series
courses.description: Top executives share insights about the healthcare industry and related career opportunities.\n

courses.subject: HL
courses.title: Delivering Value in Healthcare
courses.description: This course expands on U.S. healthcare fundamentals, introducing value-based care and examining stakeholder roles in creating value. Designed for future healthcare leaders, it emphasizes improving services through effective collaboration and responsibility across the system.

courses.subject: HL
courses.title: Healthcare Law and Ethics
courses.description: Overview of U.S. healthcare law and ethics, addressing legal issues across providers, insurers, and related organizations. Topics include patients’ rights, privacy, liability, confidentiality, licensing, healthcare reform, and other key legal aspects of the healthcare system.

courses.subject: HL
courses.title: Global Opportunities in Healthcare Leadership
courses.description: This study abroad course introduces students to global challenges and opportunities in healthcare leadership, exploring hospitals, technology, pharmaceuticals, and insurance. It examines cross-cultural differences in policy, administration, and care delivery to prepare leaders for international healthcare contexts.

courses.subject: HL
courses.title: Healthcare Research Hub
courses.description: Collaborate with faculty, students, and industry partners around the world on healthcare research. Generate knowledge on relevant healthcare industry topics based on rigorous academic research partnered with industry leaders.

courses.subject: HL
courses.title: Financing the Healthcare System
courses.description: Overview of healthcare financing, examining providers, payers, employers, individuals, and government. Topics include benchmarking, best practices, peer review, risk and performance improvement, measurement, utilization, case management, technology assessment, and decision support for future healthcare leaders.

courses.subject: HL
courses.title: Healthcare Internship
courses.description: Provide students with real-world experience in local hospitals to prepare for careers in healthcare management.
