courses.description: Analysis and design of static systems; real world problem solving; forces, moments, and vectors, equilibrium; external and internal forces; centroids and inertia; mechanical engineering fundamentals.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: New Student Seminar
courses.description: Topics of special interest to new mechanical engineering majors.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Academic Internship: International Students
courses.description: Credit is given for the documentation of work done during during an internship that is approved and provides practical experience in Mechanical Engineering.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Dynamics
courses.description: Concepts of dynamics applied to particles, systems of particles, rigid bodies, vibration systems, and nonrigid particle systems.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Leadership in a Global Context
courses.description: Principles of individual and organizational leadership in a global context. Emphasis on developing self-awareness, interpersonal skills, high-performance teams, integrity, vision and strategy. Driving forces for globalization. Valuing and leveraging diversity.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Science of Engineering Materials
courses.description: Principles and properties of solid materials and their behavior as applied to engineering.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Discovering the Field of Materials Science
courses.description: New: Interdisciplinary interactions within the materials science discipline. Mapping the path through a materials science minor. Exposure to facilities and experiential learning opportunities on campus. Preparation for post-baccalaureate employment or education in materials science.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Engineering Graphics--Principles and Applications
courses.description: Comprehensive applications of CAD-based national (ANSI) and international (ISO) graphics standards, including coordinate and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing practices, manufacturing, and product verification procedures.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Introduction to Scientific Computing and Computer-Aided Engineering
courses.description: Computer programming for engineers taught in context of solving physical systems using numerical methods. Student will program solutions using the C++ language, spreadsheets, symbolic solvers, etc.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Computational Methods in Engineering
courses.description: Numerical methods and statistics for engineers, implemented using software and computer programming
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Job Finding Skills
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to help students find success in life by learning detailed effective strategies for job finding. The course will teach students efficient techniques to obtain professional employment and will provide information on career planning, interviewing, and professionalism expected in the workplace, including ethics, diversity, and communications.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Physics and modeling of fluid flow; fluid statics, dimensional analysis, momentum, internal and external viscous flow, and fluid machinery.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (MATH 303 and ME EN 321 and ME EN 335) or (MATH 334 and ME EN 321 and ME EN 335)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Fundamentals of thermal energy and work; principle of state, conservation of mass, conservation of energy, increase of entropy principle; application to thermal and mechanical processes.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Design of Mechatronic Systems
courses.description: Microcontroller-based mechatronic systems comprised of mechanical, electrical, and software subsystems.  Electronics, printed circuit board design, microcontroller programming and interfacing, and mechanical prototyping.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Dynamic System Modeling and Analysis
courses.description: Formulating mathematical models for mechanical, electrical, fluid, and combined systems; numerical solution of motion equations; first- and second-order systems, frequency response, and transfer functions.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Conservation principles; Fundamentals of conduction, convection and radiation;  Problem solving
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Fundamentals of Biomedical Engineering
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental principles and topics of Biomedical Engineering, including Biomechanical Engineering, Biochemical Engineering, Bioinstrumentation, and Medical Imaging.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (CHEM 105 and MATH 113 and PHSCS 121) or (CHEM 105 and MATH 113 and PHSCS 106)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Engineering Measurements
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of measurement systems, characteristics of sensor signals, data acquisition, sensors, uncertainty analysis.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Mechanical System Design Fundamentals
courses.description: Static and dynamic stress and failure analysis for mechanical systems.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Manufacturing Processes
courses.description: Common manufacturing processes, including technological limitations and economic considerations. Influence of product design on process selection and manufacturing efficiency.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Applications of Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Control volume analysis; introduction to CFD; boundary layers; lift and drag, airfoils; pumps, propellers, compressors, turbines; hydroelectric and wind power generation; real world applications.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Flight Vehicle Design
courses.description: Fundamental principles for designing flight vehicles (e.g., airplanes and rockets) including introductions to aerodynamics, structures, stability, propulsion, and performance. A combination of theory, computational methods, and a design project.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Applied Thermodynamics
courses.description: Applied engineering thermodynamics including air and steam power cycles, thermodynamic relations, and introduction to combustion and equilibrium chemical reactions.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Global Perspectives on Energy and the Environment
courses.description: This course helps students appreciate the interconnection between energy and the environment and develops understanding of renewable energy technologies being deployed world-wide. The course includes course work at BYU, visits to energy sites in Utah, and travel and site visits in Europe. The travel study gives students experience with global renewable energy companies.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: Fundamental operating characteristics of internal combustion engines, spark and compression ignition. Thermodynamic cycle analysis, performance and emissions characterization, and dynamometer testing on CFR and production engines.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Gas Turbine and Jet Engine Design
courses.description: Design and synthesis of land-based and aircraft gas turbines utilizing fluid flow and thermodynamic fundamentals. Extensive discussion of turbojet, turbofan, and turboprop engines.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-EC En 483) Design of Control Systems
courses.description: Classical frequency response and time domain design of control systems. State variable control and computer simulation of control systems.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Kinematics

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Engineering Materials: Selection for Design
courses.description: Instruction emphasizes optimal materials selection techniques, practical materials-focused design, and an overview of commonly used engineering materials. These methods are applied in a practical design experience involving materials selection and manufacturing of a real product.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Materials Science Seminar
courses.description: Students will attend department or college seminars that pertain to the materials science discipline. This will expand their breadth and scope of materials science and help prepare them for graduate school or employment in materials science.\n
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Composite Material Design
courses.description: Macro- and micro-mechanical analysis and design of uni- and multidirectional composite materials.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-Phscs) Introduction to Acoustics
courses.description: Mathematical descriptions of physical phenomena in generation, propagation, and reception of acoustic waves. Fundamental acoustical instrumentation and analysis techniques. Application of physical principles and mathematical models to realistic problems.\n \n
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Mechanical Systems Design Applications
courses.description: Theory, analysis, and design of mechanical systems and components.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: This course introduces and practices the fundamental concepts of interdisciplinary market-pull innovation and entrepreneurship in a mentored setting. Interdisciplinary student teams conceive of and develop an internet-connected physical product. The double­ diamond innovation model is used, with an emphasis on prototyping and testing.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: Comprehensive two-semester design experience from conception to manufacturing planning and prototype. Product development process. Economic and manufacturing considerations. Intellectual property agreement required.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (ME EN 330 and ME EN 372 and ME EN 382) or (MFGEN 331 and MFGEN 355 and MFGEN 333)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Product Development 2 - Capstone
courses.description: Comprehensive two-semester design experience from conception to manufacturing planning and prototype. Product development process. Economic and manufacturing considerations. Intellectual property agreement required.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (ME EN 312 and ME EN 340 and ME EN 362) or (MFGEN 340 and MFGEN 401)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Singapore International Product Design and Development
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of international product development. Introduction to a structured design process. Experience working in international, multi-cultural engineering teams. Lectures, design projects, and industrial site visits in Singapore.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Manufacturing Systems Analysis and Design
courses.description: Analysis, synthesis, and control of processing and assembly operations; mathematical modeling of manufacturing processes; systems integration; applying conservation principles to processing and assembly operations.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Global Engineering Outreach Projects
courses.description: Humanitarian-based engineering and technology project development involving multi-disciplinary teams.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Mentored Learning for Undergraduate Coursework in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Selected topics in mechanical engineering.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Mentored Learning for Undergraduate Projects in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Independent learning focused on an engineering project.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (MeEn-CEEn) Design and Materials Applications
courses.description: Materials selection in design; effects of materials properties, structure and geometry on performance; process selection and property modification techniques; basics of material failure mechanism.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (MeEn-CEEn) Stress Analysis and Design of Mechanical Structures
courses.description: Stress analysis and deflection of structures; general bending and torsion, with computer applications to mechanical and aerospace structure design.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Computer Structural Analysis and Optimization
courses.description: Matrix stiffness method for 1D, 2D, and 3D skeletal structure classes. Implementing the matrix stiffness method as a computer program. Nonlinear second-order structural analysis. Structural optimization techniques including stress-ratio method, gradient-based methods, and genetic algorithms.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (MATH 302 and ME EN 372) or (MATH 213 and ME EN 372) or (CE 321 and MATH 213)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Applied Engineering Math
courses.description: Advanced engineering mathematics that builds a foundation for graduate mechanical engineering courses and research. Topics include tensor analysis, vector calculus, and solution methods for partial differential equations.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Linear Finite Element Methods
courses.description: Linear static finite element analysis of elastic solids; problem formulation, finite element discretization, and equation solving; stability, interpolation theory, and error estimates. Introduction to underlying continuum mechanics principles. Isogeometric analysis as a generalization of classical finite element analysis; basic principles of analysis-suitable computational geometry. Introduction to the industrial practice of finite element modeling leveraging commercial packages. Topics include CAD preprocessing, an overview of the mesh generation process and simulation model setup, and how to effectively use appropriate solution strategies for a given problem. Application domains include strength and durability, vibrations, transient structural dynamics, and multi-physics problems.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Structural Vibrations
courses.description: Dynamic analysis of single degree-of-freedom, discrete multi-degree-of-freedom, and continuous systems. Applications include aerospace, civil structures, and mechanical components.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Compressible Fluid Flow
courses.description: One-dimensional analysis of compressible flow with area change, friction, heat transfer, shock waves, and combined effects, including experimental methods.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Intermediate Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Fluid transport properties, review of integral analysis, Navier-Stokes equations, exact and similarity solutions, boundary layers, vorticity, jets and wakes.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Aerodynamics
courses.description: Predict aerodynamic forces and moments, like lift and drag, for 2D airfoils, 3D wings, and rotating blades across a range of Mach and Reynolds numbers. Utilize modern computational and aerodynamic methods.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: ME EN 412 or ME EN 510 or ME EN 512

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Intermediate Thermodynamics
courses.description: Review of first and second law analysis; exergy; equations of state and other thermodynamic relations; properties of mixtures and multiphase systems; chemical reactions and equilibrium.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Combustion
courses.description: Introduction to first- and second-law ideal gas combustion systems along with elementary models of homogeneous and heterogeneous premixed and/or diffusion flames.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (CHEM 105 and ME EN 340) or (CBE 373 and CBE 376)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Aircraft Structures
courses.description: Requirements, objectives, loads, materials, and tools for design of airframe structures; static behavior of thin-wall structures; durability and damage tolerance; certification and testing. Airframe component team design project.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (CCE 304 and CE 321) or (ME EN 250 and ME EN 372)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Dynamics of Mechanical Systems
courses.description: Hamiltonian and Lagrangian dynamics, generalized coordinates, linear and angular momentum, Euler angles, rigid-body motions, and gyroscopic effects. Theory taught with applications integrated.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Mechanical Vibrations
courses.description: Introduction to energy methods for system modeling, eigenvalues and mode shapes, frequency response, and spectral characterization of vibrations.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Autonomous Aircraft Guidance, Navigation, and Control
courses.description: Dynamics of fixed-wing aircraft flight, stability, and control derivatives, longitudinal and lateral control design; state-space control strategies for aircraft; and autonomous aircraft applications.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Autonomous Aircraft Guidance, Navigation, and Control
courses.description: Dynamics of fixed-wing aircraft flight, stability, and control derivatives, longitudinal and lateral control design; state-space control strategies for aircraft; and autonomous aircraft applications.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Robotics - Kinematics, Dynamics, and Control
courses.description: In this course, we cover forward and inverse kinematics for serial robot manipulators, converting joint velocities to end-effector velocity, Lagrangian and Newton-Euler treatment of robot dynamics, basic robot manipulator control techniques, and an introduction to open questions in research on serial robot manipulation.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Compliant Mechanisms
courses.description: Design and analysis of compliant mechanisms and compliant structures. Large-deflection analysis/force displacement relationships; mechanisms synthesis.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Intermediate Heat and Mass Transfer
courses.description: Analytical approaches to conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer. Introduction to mass transfer.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer
courses.description: Fluid dynamics and heat transfer analysis by numerical methods. Theory and implementation of finite difference and finite volume methods.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-EC En) Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS).
courses.description: Design, fabrication, and applications of MEMS. Mechanical properties governing their design and reliability and the processing technologies used to fabricate them.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Neuromechanics of Movement
courses.description: Biomechanics and neural control of human movement.  Principles of mechanical engineering (system dynamics, control) and physiology (motor neuroscience, musculoskeletal biomechanics) are combined to model and simulate how humans plan, control, learn, and adapt their movements.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.description: Engineering methods for modeling deformation, fracture and fatigue of materials, including metals, polymers, composites and ceramics. Deformation modes include elastic, plastic, viscoelastic and creep.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Kinetics of Materials
courses.description: A unified treatment of kinetic processes in materials,including transport, chemical reactions, phase transformations, and microstructure evolution. Emphasis is placed on crystalline materials, but application to glasses, polymers and other material systems are discussed throughout. Specific topics include: kinetic theory of gases,rate theory, reaction kinetics, irreversible thermodynamics,diffusion in a broad spectrum of material classes (both atomistic mechanisms and phenomenological/continuum level models), influence of defects of diffusion, evolution of surfaces, phase transformations (solidification, nucleation and growth, spinodal decomposition), coarsening, grain growth, and morphological instabilities.  \n
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Biomechanical Engineering
courses.description: Mechanics of biological systems.  A continuum mechanics-based approach to the structure, function, mechanical response, and active remodeling of hard and soft tissues of the body.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Materials Modeling: Methods in Atomistic, Mesoscale, and Continuum Simulations
courses.description: Theory and application of various computer simulations to model, understand, and predict the properties of real materials.  Specific topics include: first-principles atomistic models, empirical potential atomistic models, mesoscale models, and continuum finite element analysis.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (ME EN 250 and ME EN 273) or (ME EN 250 and ME EN 275)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Materials in Extreme Environments
courses.description: This class introduces students to models and empirical data that predict safe operational ranges for materials in high temperature, irradiated, and corrosive environments.\nMethods to measure material properties and performance in each environment are discussed, as well as the fundamental mechanisms that cause changes in material properties. \n
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Metallurgy
courses.description: Fundamental principles of physical metallurgy and their application to design.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.title: (Me En-Phscs) Fundamentals of Acoustics.
courses.description: Vibrating systems, elastic media, mechanical energy, and radiation. Sound generation, transmission, reflection, and reception.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Computer-Aided Engineering Software Development
courses.description: Programming methods for development of engineering software. Data structures, architecture, libraries, and graphical user interfaces, with applications to CAD systems.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Design for Additive Manufacturing
courses.description: This course explores the past, present, and future of additive manufacturing (AM), including how it enables mass customization and increased design complexity. Lab experiences focus on preparing 3D models, operating several types of AM systems, and post processing finished parts. Students apply "Design for AM" principles to adapt existing part designs for AM and design new products that capitalize on the possibilities only available through AM.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (ME EN 250 and MFGEN 140) or (ME EN 250 and ME EN 272)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Design of Medical Devices
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course aims to provide a comprehensive and practical understanding of the design, development, and deployment of medical devices. Rooted in mechanical engineering, the course integrates key principles from biomedicine, materials science, quality assurance, and intellectual property law. With a focus on real-world application, students will engage in case studies, a hands-on project, and team-based design exercises that simulate the challenges and opportunities within the medical device industry.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Optimization Techniques in Engineering.
courses.description: Application of computational optimization techniques to constrained engineering design.  Theory and application of gradient-based and gradient-free algorithms for unconstrained and constrained nonlinear problems.  Robust design methods.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Product Design
courses.description: Emerging design methodology and design strategies for complex systems, including decomposition methods and sensitivity analysis. Advanced CAD/CAE/CAM technologies applied to design.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Uncertainty Quantification
courses.description: The theory and practice of for assessing the influence of uncertainty on the behavior of systems, models, and corresponding predictions. Students will apply uncertainty quantification methods to example models and a system/model of their choice.   \n
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Systems Engineering and CAD Applications
courses.description: Principles and practices involved in systems engineering and design with related applications in advanced CAD models generation, optimization, and automation.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (ME EN 273 and ME EN 475 and STAT 201) or (ME EN 275 and ME EN 475 and STAT 201)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Global Product Development
courses.description: Preparing students to be leaders in globally-influenced product development organizations.  Includes visits to U.S. and overseas companies and universities.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Deep Learning for Engineers
courses.description: Design and implement neural networks in an engineering context. Focus on unique architectures and approaches for engineers which incorporate prior physical knowledge, domain constraints, and established scientific algorithms.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: Design and analysis of advanced composite structures; deflections, buckling, and vibration of thin plates and sandwich plates; design guidelines; design examples; project.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Continuum and Solid Mechanics
courses.description: Derivation of partial differential equations of continuum mechanics. Closed-form solution of classical problems in elasticity. Theory of beams, plates, and axisymmetric shells with closed-form solutions. Large displacement strain tensors, stress tensors, equilibrium equations, beam theory, and plate theory. Constitutive theory including nonlinear elasticity, viscoelasticity, plasticity, and hyperelasticity.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (Me En-CE En) Nonlinear Finite Element Methods
courses.description: Nonlinear dynamic finite element analysis of solids.  Nonlinear continuum mechanics, finite element formulation, and elementary solution algorithms for nonlinear algebraic problems. focusing on hyperelastic solids.  Advanced topics in isogeometric analysis, computational analysis-suitable geometry, and adaptivity.  An introduction to dynamics; basic methods of time integration, such
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: (MeEn-CEEn) Spectral Analysis of Dynamic Systems
courses.description: Digital signal processing and analysis applied to computer-aided testing, system identification, and characterization of random processes. Applications include vibration and acoustic testing, seismic recording and analysis, and system identification for control.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Turbulence
courses.description: Introduction to turbulence, flow instability and transition, concept of scale, Reynolds averaging, wall-bounded and free shear flows, closure modes, and measurement techniques.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: Fluid dynamics of the atmosphere and oceans related to free surface, two layer, and continuously stratified flows emphasizing linear and nonlinear free-surface and internal gravity waves.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: Experimental methods for analyzing fluid flow and heat transfer. Theory and application of techniques in velocimetry, pressure sensing, thermometry, and flow visualization.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Advanced Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: Detailed combustion analysis of compression and spark ignition engines. Modeling concepts from zero to multidimensional. Engine heat transfer and I.C. engine diagnostics.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Robotic Localization and Mapping
courses.description: Mobile robotic systems depend on the ability to perceive their environment, determine their location, and build up a model of their surroundings. These tasks must be accomplished simultaneously and in real-time while taking into account the effects of uncertainty due to noisy sensors, incorrect models, and complex unstructured environments. In this class, we will explore fundamental and modern algorithms and solutions to robotic mapping and localization.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.prerequisites_text: (MATH 213 and MATH 314 and MATH 334) or (MATH 302 and MATH 303)

courses.subject: ME EN
courses.title: Radiative Heat Transfer
courses.description: Advanced engineering analysis of radiant heat exchange between surfaces, in enclosures, and in absorbing, emitting, and scattering media.

courses.description: Advanced engineering analysis of convective heat transfer in internal and external laminar and turbulent flows.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: Representations of inhomogenous material microstructure, crystallography, orientation distribution functions, Fourier representations, bounding theories for defect-insensitive properties, grain boundaries and grain boundary engineering, microstructure sensitive design.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: Advanced mechanics of biological systems. A continuum mechanics-based approach to the structure, function, mechanical response, and active remodeling of hard and soft tissues of the body.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.title: (Me En-EC En 774) Non-Linear System Theory
courses.description: Mathematical introduction to non-linear dynamic systems. Topics include Lyapunov methods, passivity, input-output stability, and non-linear feedback design.

courses.description: Exploring the rise of Islam, the life of Muhammad, basic beliefs and practices, major figures and movements, and contemporary political and social issues.

courses.subject: MESA

courses.description: Focus on the following topics, with application to training in Middle East Studies: career exploration, internship planning, graduate school exploration and planning, developing a professional resume and web presence, and career networking.??Students will attend several career-related lectures of their choosing, and complete assignments designed to support their professional development after graduation.

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: The Qur'an in English
courses.description: Students examine and assess interpretations of the Qur'an in English, studying the historical, theological, and literary aspects of the Qur'anic text. \n\n

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: Islam in Contemporary Society
courses.description: Islam in modern society: doctrine, practices, institutions, approaches to the challenges of modern life; the rise of fundamentalism.

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: Middle Eastern Field Studies
courses.description: Topics include the history, archeology, religion, society, and politics of the region. Visit key sites described in both the Old and New Testaments, monuments of the Hebrew and Roman worlds, as well as sites of historical and contemporary social and political relevance. Assess the rich historical and spiritual legacy of biblical Israel, patterns of political and social development in the 20th century, including the founding of the state of Israel. Examine the history of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, contemporary domestic social and political issues in Israel and Palestine, attempts at conflict resolution, and opportunities for future political development.

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: Directed Middle East Study
courses.description: Study and research in the Middle East.

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: Academic Internship
courses.description: Individualized work or volunteer experience in the Middle East or with an organization dealing with the Middle East.  Must be coordinated through International Study Programs or the Washington Seminar and with the consent of the Middle East Studies/Arabic  coordinator.

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: Topics in Middle East Studies
courses.description: Topics vary.

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: Capstone Arabic
courses.description: Readings in Arabic texts supporting research for the MESA capstone seminar.

courses.subject: MESA
courses.title: Senior Seminar in Middle East Studies
courses.description: Capstone course, including major research paper demonstrating ability to integrate cross-disciplinary information and methodology.

courses.description: This course will introduce students to a manufacturing engineering design process, technical sketching, parametric modeling and design, tolerance specification, documentation drawing and assembly modeling.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: MFGEN

courses.description: Methods and procedures to shape materials using basic machine tools; cutting theory, tool selection, metrology methods, and machine operation. Introduction to computer numerical control.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: MFGEN
courses.title: Computer-Aided Manufacturing
courses.description: Manual and computer-assisted programming of computer numerical controlled (CNC) equipment. Developing CNC programs to manufacture parts for high production.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: MFGEN
courses.title: Manufacturing Leadership
courses.description: Lectures on personal and professional development, ethics, global leadership, and belonging. An emphasis on resumes and internship preparation will be included.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: MFGEN
courses.title: Manufacturing Electronics and Microsystems
courses.description: Basics of electricity; behavior and manufacture of resistors, inductors, capacitors, transformers; motors; manufacture of transistors, ICs, MCMs, circuit boards. Computers; digital communications; networking.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering
courses.department: Electrical and Computer Engineering, Department of

courses.subject: MFGEN
courses.title: Metals Processes
courses.description: Capabilities and applications of common metal-processing methods, including relationships between part design, material, and process parameters.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: MFGEN

courses.description: Application of sensors, actuators, robotics, part feeding and assembly, PLCs, pneumatic and hydraulic control, for justifying industrial automation.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.description: Tools and principles of quality in manufacturing systems based on the Six Sigma process. Basic tools, variation, loss function, cost of quality, SPC, DOE, and FMEA. Comprehensive project required.
courses.college: Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering

courses.subject: MFGEN

courses.description: Understanding plastic materials, properties, and uses. Survey of plastic-manufacturing processes. Designing plastic products and manufacturing systems.

courses.description: This course provides a mentored, faculty-student experience to better prepare students considering a PhD in public and nonprofit management and/or policy.

courses.subject: MPA
courses.title: Nonprofit Organization Management
courses.description: Orient students to principles of best practice in the management of nonprofit organizations. courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.description: Introduction to the dynamic world of local government. Topics include forms of government, political relationships and policy making, and issues of service delivery.

courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: MPA

courses.department: Public Service and Ethics, Romney Institute of

courses.subject: MSB

courses.description: Lecture series exploring Marriott School undergraduate business programs.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Academic Internship
courses.description: Supervised experience for Pre-Business students in business related work. Opportunity to link learning with practical field applications.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Applying Business Foundations
courses.description: Explore why and how people interact in organizations. Apply and integrate foundational business principles and skills to ethically and effectively lead and improve businesses and nonprofits, products and services, communities and families, teams and individuals.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Planning for Financial Security at Retirement
courses.description: Fundamentals of good financial management necessary for successful retirement.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Financial Management
courses.description: Financial statement analysis, financial planning, sources of financing, working capital management, risk and return, and valuation.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Leadership and the Gospel of Jesus Christ
courses.description: Introduction to leadership in principles, practice, and lives of leaders—especially lives of students. Examine leadership as an important dimension of becoming a disciple of Jesus Christ and study personal and organizational aspects of leadership.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Becoming a Disciple Leader
courses.description: Capstone designed to help students discover leadership capabilities and develop ability to lead as a disciple of Jesus Christ. Application of principles of leadership and of the Gospel. Discover personal strengths, gifts, and missions, and develop skills and commitments essential for working with and through others to improve organizations of all kinds-families, Church, work, and communities.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Negotiation
courses.description: Skills based negotiation class taught in an interactive workshop format. Frameworks for how to prepare, conduct and debrief negotiations will be taught. Students will learn to negotiate in both professional and personal settings.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Introductory Business Analytics
courses.description: Fundamental principles and skills for data preparation, data visualization, and regression analysis using analytics software.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Career Development and Student Mentoring
courses.description: Introduction to the resources, services, and opportunities for career development available to business management majors. Specific projects include developing a career plan, refining interviewing and networking skills, and interacting individually with a mentor well-established in a directly relevant career.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: GlobalHub
courses.description: GlobalHub gives students hands-on experience creating global business content, leading marketing campaigns, and organizing events. Teams specialize in strategy, production, or events, gaining cross-cultural communication, media management skills, and a portfolio of real-world work.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Product Management
courses.description: Introduces product-strategy skills, including market analysis and product development/launch/lifecycle management, with a focus on cross-functional collaboration with UX, design, engineering, marketing, sales, operations, and support to effectively meet customer needs.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Product Career Lecture Series
courses.description: Lectures by product management professionals to introduce students to nature of work and opportunities in the field.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Professional Ethics
courses.description: Analyzing ethical dilemmas and understanding ethical theories as they apply to decision making in management.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Executive Lectures
courses.description: Lectures by top executives on subjects significant to executive leadership.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Leading with Purpose
courses.description: Learn how to grow as a purpose-driven leader by looking at lessons from business leaders who exemplify Christlike attributes. We'll explore how business can make money and also transform the world for good. You’ll be able to identify an organization’s purpose, build a strategy around that purpose, and create a company culture to fulfill that purpose.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Leadership Development
courses.description: Principles and practices to help students become Christlike leaders in their homes, the Church, communities, and other organizations. Focuses on key leadership models, leading with Christlike attributes, performance management, defining vision/strategy, influence, and self-awareness.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: Introduction to International Business
courses.description: Complexities confronting U.S. firms and their management in international environments. Emphasizes functional and planning areas, including organization, market research, financial analysis.

courses.subject: MSB
courses.title: International Business and Culture
courses.description: Understand how national culture influences make international business interactions successful and how decision making is impacted based upon global cultural differences.

courses.description: Direct, practical on-campus (not in the field) professional experience consulting with established and startup companies and organizations.  Students are accepted to work on specific projects based on their skills, interests, and major emphasis.  Students apply to be involved in specific projects.

courses.description: How corporate boards are led, focusing especially on the role of the director, the rights of shareholders, the compensation of executives, and the challenge boards face in balancing the needs of shareholders, managers, and other stakeholders.

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematics Education
courses.description: Introduction to the field of mathematics education. Background on the nature of mathematics, its teaching and learning. Program and teacher certification requirements are also discussed.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Critical Review of School Mathematics
courses.description: Strengthen understanding of middle-school mathematics with an emphasis on multiplicative structures, proportionality and linearity; gain awareness as mathematics learners in learning communities; learn how to support collaborative communities as teachers.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Exploration of Mathematics Teaching
courses.description: Field-based initial teaching experience directed at helping prospective teachers experience demands and opportunities associated with teaching mathematics to secondary students.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences
courses.prerequisites_text: (MATH 213 and MATH 290 and MTHED 177) or (MATH 290 and MATH 313 and MTHED 177)

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Task Design for Student Learning
courses.description: Strengthen understanding of high-school mathematics, with an emphasis on algebra and functions, in the context of selecting, modifying, and creating tasks that support students' development of both conceptual understanding and procedural fluency.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Assessment of Student Learning
courses.description: Strengthen understanding of high-school mathematics, with an emphasis on transformational geometry and trigonometry, in the context of creating and critiquing formative and summative assessments that support students' development of both conceptual understanding and procedural fluency.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: History and Philosophy of Mathematics.
courses.description: Historical development of important mathematical ideas and philosophies; implications for the mathematical curriculum.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Teaching Statistics and Probability
courses.description: Exploration of important conceptual underpinnings, common misconceptions and students' ways of thinking, appropriate use of technology, and instructional practices to support and assess the learning of probability and statistics.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Basic Concepts of Mathematics
courses.description: Concept-oriented exploration of counting, number, and operations in relation to children's learning.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Concepts of Mathematics
courses.description: Concept-oriented exploration of rational numbers and informal geometry in relation to children's learning.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Mathematics Teaching with Technology
courses.description: Examining technological tools that illustrate mathematical concepts and assist in solving mathematics problems. Using technology tools to investigate modeling, highlight mathematical relationships, and motivate proof. Additionally, exploring and creating algorithms, functions, constructions, and transformations.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Survey of Geometry
courses.description: Logical and historical development of Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, transformations and symmetry; relationships among axiomatic systems; use of software and other geometric models; proofs and Van Hiele levels.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Mathematics Teaching in the Public Schools
courses.description: Developing skill in designing and implementing lesson plans that include high-cognitive demand tasks; anticipating, monitoring, and building on student mathematical thinking; and orchestrating mathematical discussions that lead to student understanding of fundamental mathematics concepts.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Practicum in Mathematics Education
courses.description: Observing secondary mathematics classrooms as a means of reflecting on teaching practices that support student learning of fundamental mathematical concepts, including use of high-cognitive demand tasks and orchestration of mathematical discussions as well as eliciting, making sense of, and building on student mathematical thinking.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Secondary Student Teaching in Mathematics
courses.description: Capstone, field-based, semester-long experience in teaching mathematics to secondary students; demonstrating proficiency in all program standards.  Seminar required.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Secondary Minor Student Teaching
courses.description: Supervised, full-day, four week experience to develop and demonstrate competence in teaching minor area course content in the secondary classroom.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Readings in Mathematics Education
courses.description: Directed readings beyond scope of usual undergraduate courses.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Academic Internship: Secondary Mathematics Education
courses.description: Capstone, field-based, semester-long experience in teaching mathematics to secondary students; demonstrating proficiency in all program standards. Seminar required.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED

courses.description: Undergraduate research experience.  Faculty-supervised research.  Written and oral presentation of findings required.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.description: (Math-Chem-C S-Geol-MthEd-Phscs-Stat) Introduction for science, math, and statistics majors to careers in industry. Project planning, oral and written business presentations, business accounting, and technology readiness.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Problem Solving
courses.description: Solving and building explanations and presenting solutions to conceptually important problems. Analyzing research on problem solving and its role in teaching and learning mathematics.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Euclidean Geometry:  Content, Learning, and Teaching
courses.description: Euclidean geometry, including classical problems, polyhedra, transformations, congruence, similarity, integer geometry, minimization; technology in geometry, Van Hiele levels, role of proof, and high school curriculum.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Foundational Issues in Learning Mathematics
courses.description: Introduction to research in mathematics learning; mathematical thinking; cognitive, social, and philosophical approaches to describing mathematics learning.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED

courses.description: Introduction to scholarly inquiry in mathematics education; issues in research methodology.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Topics in Mathematics Education
courses.description: Includes specific research areas and curriculum studies of school mathematics topics (i.e. geometry, algebra, and calculus).
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Technology for Learning and Teaching Mathematics
courses.description: Analyzing research relative to learning mathematics with technology; exploring mathematical problems using technology; design curriculum; conducting research in the learning and teaching of mathematics with technology.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Graduate Student Seminar
courses.description: Reading, discussing, and writing about relevant public discourse, policies, and issues in the broad arena of mathematics education.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Number and Number Sense
courses.description: Research on children's understanding of early numbers, number operations, number sense, multidigit arithmetic, fractions, decimals, and proportions.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Algebraic Reasoning
courses.description: Fundamental concepts (e.g., variables, equality, pattern recognition, function, covariation, equations), processes (e.g., mathematizing, generalizing, modeling), and research in algebraic reasoning.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Calculus Teaching and Learning
courses.description: Fundamental calculus concepts as well as the curricula, reform efforts, and research associated with teaching and learning calculus.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: MTHED
courses.title: Mathematics Teaching and Teacher Education
courses.description: Exploration of the research on mathematics teaching, teacher preparation, and teacher professional development.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.title: Policies and Laws of Aquatic Systems
courses.description:
This course provides students an appreciation of how state, federal, and international law relates to aquatic and terresrial systems and species, sometimes protecting them and sometimes harming them. Students will understand how the law addresses or fails to address major challenges facing these systems and species. It will also create a more nuanced understanding of some of the competing interests that also garner policy support.
 
The course will provide an introduction to water and land use law, federal lands law, Superfund, the Clean Water Act, the Endangered Species Act, the public trust doctrine, international water disputes and management, and the Coastal Zone Management Act. It also provides students with a more nuanced understanding of how the National Environmental Policy Act relates to this context.

courses.description: Specific and predominate social work direct practice theories and models applied to counseling and with clinical populations.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.description: Integrated seminar experience that links group work theory and practice incorporating social work ethics and values. courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.description: Empowering and engaging with communities and organizations to address social problems and improve organizational functioning utilizing effective leadership strategies.

courses.description: Knowledge and skills necessary to apply appropriate strategies for treating disorders, including depression, anxiety, substance use, and trauma.  Exploration of the relationship between assessment and treatment, and the need for accountability in direct social work practice.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.description: Social work knowledge and practice skills needed to engage, assess, and intervene with children, adolescents, and their families. Evidence-based practices adapted for children, including a comprehensive bio-psycho-social-spiritual and developmental assessment, are considered. Focus on models for intervening with common mental illnesses, trauma, and family and peer difficulties typical of this age group.

courses.description: Full spectrum of substance use interventions: intervening for treating substance use disorders with selected special populations.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.description: Interface of religious and social work values, attitudes, and principles.

courses.description: Current problems and treatments in social work practice.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: SOC W
courses.title: Motivational Interviewing
courses.description: Motivational interviewing (MI) is a collaborative and goal-oriented counseling style designed to increase motivation and commitment in clients. MI is well suited for clients who are ambivalent about making personal or lifestyle changes because the counselor helps the client make their own argument for change. This course is intended to provide students with a thorough and practical introduction to this counseling approach.
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.subject: SOC W
courses.title: Trauma-Informed Clinical Social Work Practice
courses.description: How to work effectively with clients who have experienced trauma. Viewing client mental distress symptoms through a trauma lens, and preparation to work with clients who have experienced diverse forms of trauma. Upon completion, students will receive multiple online trauma certificates, including, but not limited to TF-CBT and CPT from MUSC (Medical University of South Carolina) and complex trauma; secondary traumatic stress; culture and trauma; family systems; terrorism, disaster and children; and military families through the National Child Traumatic Stress Network (NCTSN).
courses.college: College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences

courses.description: Development of interpersonal and presentational speaking skills in Spanish at the ACTFL Advanced Mid to Advanced High level. Not for native speakers.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Third-Year Spanish Reading, Grammar, and Culture
courses.description: Intensive study and practice with Spanish grammar, vocabulary, and writings incorporating cultural and literary readings.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Third-Year Spanish Composition
courses.description: Study and practice of different writing styles, developing research skills.

courses.title: Cultures of Spanish America

courses.subject: SPAN

courses.description: Exploration of theory and practical applications of Spanish to English translation and interpretation, with practice in translating various textual genres.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: English to Spanish Translation
courses.description: Exploration of theory and practical applications of English to Spanish translation, with attention to translating specialized texts and developing knowledge of the translation industry.

Key topics include standards-based lesson planning/curriculum development, use of technology, performance-based assessment, and addressing student diversity.

courses.description: Historical and theoretical trends in language teaching; standards- and proficiency-based lesson planning; strategies for teaching in the target language; teaching of interpersonal and presentational speaking skills; contextualized approaches for teaching grammar, and vocabulary; strategies for developing intercultural competence; and development of skills in general educational technologies common across disciplines. First of a two-semester sequence for Spanish Teaching majors and minors; fulfills methods course requirement for Dual Language Immersion Teaching minors.

courses.description: Innovative approaches to unit planning; teaching of interpretive reading and listening skills; teaching of presentational writing skills; assessing language and culture learning; enhancing instruction with technology; adapting instruction for diverse learners; and becoming a professionally-engaged language educator. Second course in a two-semester sequence for Spanish Teaching majors and minors.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Practicum in Teaching Spanish
courses.description: Implementing meaningful and engaging instruction for secondary students in Spanish; developing critical thinking, problem solving, literacy, and democratic character; assessing learner performance.

courses.title: Academic Internship: Spanish Language Field Experience

courses.subject: SPAN

courses.description: Fourth-year study of Spanish grammar and usage.

courses.description: The linguistic study of Spanish as it varies regionally, socially, and situationally (language variation) and how/why Spanish is changing through time (language change).

courses.subject: SPAN

courses.subject: SPAN

courses.description: Selected Spanish-American novelists such as Juan Rulfo, Gabriel Garcia Marquez, Alejo Carpentier, Mario Vargas-Llosa, etc.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish-American Poetry.
courses.description: Selected Spanish-American poets, movements, and national traditions.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish American Drama
courses.description: Twentieth-century theatre from Spanish America and Brazil.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultures of Spanish America
courses.description: An in-depth examination of some aspect of Spanish American culture and civilization. Subject matter will vary. This course is recommended for those individuals who may already have a broad exposure to the culture and civilization of the Spanish-speaking countries of the Americas and/or those who desire a more focused cultural experience.

courses.subject: SPAN

courses.description: Introduction and development of an important literary genre in Spanish America, including works of Jorge Luis Borges, Julio Cortazar, Juan Rulfo, Gabriel Garcia Marquez, etc.

courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Applied Regression and Generalized Linear Models
courses.description: This course introduces key tools for building and evaluating statistical models used in real-world data analysis. Students will learn how to apply and interpret linear and generalized linear models, assess model fit, and use modern techniques like regularization and flexible modeling. The course emphasizes practical data analysis, clear communication of results, and ethical statistical practice. It is designed to help students bridge the gap between applied work and statistical theory while building a broad foundation in modeling methods.
courses.college: College of Computational, Mathematical, & Physical Sciences

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Experimental Design and Causal Inference
courses.description: This course equips students with the skills to design robust experiments and apply causal inference techniques to answer research questions.  Topics include experimental and quasi-experimental designs, confounding, and bias.  Emphasis is placed on practical applications using statistical software and effective communication of findings, blending classical design principles with modern causal inference methods.

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Statistical and Machine Learning
courses.description: This course introduces foundational concepts and methods in statistical machine learning, with an emphasis on supervised and unsupervised learning, optimization, and model assessment. Topics include decision trees, ensemble methods, support vector machines, neural networks, clustering, and dimension reduction, along with interpretability and ethical considerations. Students will implement models using modern statistical software, develop reproducible workflows, and explore the theoretical principles guiding modern machine learning approaches.

courses.description: An in-depth study of modern statistical modeling techniques, emphasizing multivariate distribution theory, likelihood-based inference, and extensions of the linear model. courses.description:
This course is a writing seminar designed to help students learn to prepare for and write a master’s thesis AND to become better academic writers overall.  Academic writing can be a new form of writing for many students and they need assistance in order to successfully express their ideas in academic settings.
This course will emphasize a variety of topics including how to write a research question, how to write a problem statement and rationale for a study, how to craft a purpose for the study, how to conduct, synthesize, and write a review of the literature, how to use APA formatting appropriately to improve academic writing skills.

courses.description: This course offered in conjunction with the Media Arts program's study abroad program will expose students to renowned repertory programs, thorough retrospectives, and the most wide-ranging commercially distributed film offerings in the world. We will enjoy the films themselves along with a host of exemplary scholarly resources (lectures, artist interviews, scholarly notes) from nation-specific institutes of film education. In addition, our program will be distinguished by its emphasis on the ancestor arts and by its access to some of the world's great art institutions. Film is a combination and occasionally a culmination of the arts preceding it. In that spirit, film practitioners as well as students of the arts will be enriched and deepened by their exposure to our host city's rich history and its vast supply of great plays, paintings, buildings, landscapes, and design.

courses.subject: WRTG
courses.title: Writing and Rhetoric
courses.description: Writing and research with a focus on inquiry, information literacy, rhetorical awareness, genre knowledge, and reflection. Emphasizes writing as a flexible process and writers as curious, open, and charitable.

courses.subject: WRTG
courses.title: Writing about the Arts and Humanities
courses.description: Writing for both academic and mass audiences about the functions, meanings, values, and qualities of art and the humanities. Library research paper.

courses.subject: WRTG
courses.title: Persuasive Writing
courses.description: Expository and persuasive writing focusing on practical reasons for evaluating audiences, generating and structuring an argument, and making stylistic decisions. Library research paper.

courses.subject: WRTG
courses.title: Advanced Writing for Educators
courses.description: Writing 313 is an advanced course in composition with the purpose of teaching research, writing, and oral communication skills needed for careers in education and teaching.

courses.subject: WRTG
courses.title: Writing in the Social Sciences
courses.description: Writing characteristic of disciplines that inquire into human behavior and institutions; correspondence, proposals, library paper, empirical research, and reviews.

courses.subject: WRTG
courses.title: Technical Communication
courses.description: Effective processes of written, oral, and visual technical communication, including collaborative processes. Writing for academic and professional audiences.
